The first eleven verses of it   David delivered to Asaph, ( I Chronicles 16:7 , &c.)   to be used in the daily service of the sanctuary.   Here is the preface, ver. 1-7.   The history itself in several articles: God's covenant with the   patriarchs, ver. 8-11.   His care of them in a strange land, ver. 12-15.   His raising up Joseph, ver. 16-22.   The increase of Israel in Egypt, and their deliverance out of   it, ver. 23-38.   His care of them in the wilderness, and their settlement in Canaan,   ver. 39-45.

title: Psalms 105:3
text: V. 3. Glory-Glory in the God whom you serve, as the only true God.

title: Psalms 105:4
text: V. 4. Seek-The Lord in his strength, in his sanctuary, or before the ark, which is called God's strength.  Face-His gracious presence.

title: Psalms 105:5
text: V.5. Judgments-The punishments which he brought upon Egypt by his mere word.

title: Psalms 105:6
text: V. 6. Of Jacob-The only branch of Abraham's seed to whom the following blessings belong.

title: Psalms 105:7
text: V. 7. Judgments-God executes his judgments upon all nations and people.

title: Psalms 105:8
text: V. 8. Remembered-So as to perform it.  The word-The promise. Commanded-Established.  Thousand generations-To all generations.

title: Psalms 105:9
text: V. 9. Oath-Wherewith he ratified the covenant with Isaac,  Genesis 26:3 .

title: Psalms 105:10
text: V. 10. A law-That it might be as firm and irrevocable as a law.

title: Psalms 105:11
text: V. 11. Lot-The portion assigned to you by lot.

title: Psalms 105:13
text: V. 13. They went-Both in Canaan, where there were seven nations, and in Egypt.

title: Psalms 105:15
text: V. 15. Anointed-My prophets, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; who are called God's anointed, because they were consecrated to be his peculiar people, and to be kings and princes in their families. And they are called prophets, because God familiarly conversed with them and revealed his will to them, and by them to others.

title: Psalms 105:16
text: V. 16. Staff of bread-Bread, which is the staff or support of our lives.

title: Psalms 105:19
text: V. 19. His word-That word or revelation which came first to Pharaoh in a dream, and then to Joseph concerning the interpretation of it. Purged-From those calamities which were cast upon him, and so prepared the way for his release.

title: Psalms 105:23
text: V. 23. Ham-Ham was the father of Mizraim, or the Egyptians,  Genesis 10:6 .

title: Psalms 105:25
text: V. 25. Turned-That is, suffered them, to be turned.

title: Psalms 105:28
text: V. 28. They-Moses and Aaron, who inflicted that plague after Pharaoh had threatened them.

title: Psalms 105:30
text: V. 30. Land-Their country. In chambers-Which entered into the chambers. Kings-Of Pharaoh and his sons, and his chief nobles and governors.

title: Psalms 105:31
text: V. 31. Coasts-In all their land, even to the utmost borders of it.

title: Psalms 105:37
text: V. 37. Feeble-Diseased or unable for his journey: which in so vast a body, and in a people who had been so dreadfully oppressed, was wonderful.

title: Psalms 105:39
text: V. 39. Covering-To protect them from the heat of the sun.

title: Psalms 105:40
text: V. 40. Quails-He speaks of the first giving of quails,  Exodus 16:13 , which God gave them as a refreshment, notwithstanding their sin in desiring them, which he graciously pardoned. Bread-With manna which came out of the air, commonly called heaven.

title: Psalms 105:41
text: V. 41. River-They flowed in channels which God provided for them, and followed the Israelites in their march.

title: Psalms 105:44
text: V. 44. Labour-The fruits of their labour; their cities, vineyards, olive-yards.

title: Psalms 106:1
text:
PSALM CVI. 
 
  The foregoing psalm was an history of God's goodness to Israel;   this is an history of their rebellion: against him; probably both   were wrote by David at the same time, as we find the first verse   and the two last in that psalm, which he delivered to Asaph,    I Chronicles 16:35 , &c.   Herein we have the preface, ver. 1-5.   The narrative of all of the sins of Israel, aggravated by the great   things God did for them; their provocations at the Red-sea, ver. 6-12.   Lusting, ver. 13-15.   Mutinying, ver. 16-18.   Worshiping the golden calf, ver. 19-23.   Murmuring, ver. 24-27.   Worshiping Baal-peor, ver. 28-31.   Quarreling with Moses, ver, 32, 33.   Mixing with the nations of Canaan, ver. 34-39.   God rebuked them, yet saved them from ruin, ver. 40-46.   The conclusion, ver. 47, 48.   It begins and ends with Hallelujah.

title: Psalms 106:4
text: V. 4. Me-He speaks here in the name, and on the behalf of the whole nation.  With-With those favours which thou dost usually and peculiarly give to thy people.

title: Psalms 106:5
text: V. 5. See-Enjoy.  Chosen-Of thy chosen people; such as are Israelites indeed.  Gladness-Such joy as thou hast formerly afforded unto thy beloved nation.  Glory-That we may have occasion to glory in God's goodness towards us.   Inheritance-In the congregation of thy people.

title: Psalms 106:6
text: V. 6. Glory-As our fathers did.

title: Psalms 106:7
text: V. 7. At the sea-When those wonders were but newly done, and fresh in memory.

title: Psalms 106:8
text: V. 8. Saved them-That he may vindicate his name from the blasphemous reproaches, which would have been cast upon it, if they had been destroyed.

title: Psalms 106:9
text: V. 9. Led them-As securely as if they had walked upon the dry land.

title: Psalms 106:13
text: V. 13. Soon-Even within three days,  Exodus 15:22 Exodus 15:23 . Waited not-They did not wait patiently upon God for supplies, in such manner and time as he thought fit.

title: Psalms 106:14
text: V. 14. Lusted-For flesh.

title: Psalms 106:15
text: V. 15. Souls-Into their bodies.  So their inordinate desire of pampering their bodies, was the occasion of destroying them.

title: Psalms 106:16
text: V. 16. The saint-So called, because he was consecrated by God for that sacred office of the priesthood, in which respect all the priests are said to be holy,  Leviticus 21:6-8 .  Hereby he intimates, that their envy and rebellion was not only against Aaron, but against God himself.

title: Psalms 106:19
text: V. 19. A calf-When they were but just brought out of Egypt by such wonders, and had seen the plagues of God upon the Egyptian idolaters, and when the law of God was but newly delivered to them in such a tremendous manner.

title: Psalms 106:20
text: V. 20. Their glory-God, who was indeed their glory.  Into-Into the golden image of an ox or calf, which is so far from feeding his people, as the true God did the Israelites, that he must be fed by them.

title: Psalms 106:23
text: V. 23. Breach-God had made a wall about them; but they had made a breach in it by their sins, at which the Lord, who was now justly become their enemy, might enter to destroy them; which he had certainly done, if Moses by his prevailing intercession had not hindered him.

title: Psalms 106:24
text: V. 24. Despised-Preferring Egypt, and their former bondage, before it,  Numbers 14:3 Numbers 14:4 .

title: Psalms 106:25
text: V. 25. The voice-To God's command, that they should boldly enter into it.

title: Psalms 106:26
text: V. 26. Lifted up-He sware.  Of this dreadful and irrevocable oath of God, see  Numbers 14:11 Numbers 14:12 .

title: Psalms 106:27
text: V. 27. Overthrow-He sware also (tho' not at the same time) that he would punish their sins, not only in their persons, but in their posterity.

title: Psalms 106:28
text: V. 28. Joined-They had communion with him, as God's people have with God in acts of his worship.

title: Psalms 106:31
text: V. 31. And-It was accepted and rewarded of God as an act of justice and piety.

title: Psalms 106:37
text: V. 37. Devils-They did not worship God as they pretended, but devils in their idols; for those spirits, which were supposed by the Heathen idolaters to inhabit in their images, were not good spirits, but evil spirits, or devils.

title: Psalms 106:43
text: V. 43. Counsel-By forsaking God's way, and following their own inventions.

title: Psalms 106:45
text: V. 45. Repented-Changed his course and dealing with them.

title: Psalms 107:1
text:
PSALM CVII. 
 
  The psalmist here observes God's providential care of the children of   men in general, and shews how he helps those that are in any distress,   in answer to their prayers.   He instances in banishment and dispersion, ver. 1-9.   Captivity and imprisonment, ver. 10-16.   Sickness, ver. 17-22.   Distress at sea, ver. 23-32.   The disposal of families and nations, ver. 33-13

title: Psalms 107:3
text: V. 3. Gathered-Into their own land.

title: Psalms 107:4
text: V. 4. No city-Or rather, no town inhabited, where they might refresh themselves.

title: Psalms 107:6
text: V. 6. The Lord-Heb. Unto Jehovah, to the true God. For the Heathens had, many of them, some knowledge of the true God.

title: Psalms 107:7
text: V. 7. Forth-Out of the wilderness.

title: Psalms 107:10
text: V. 10. Darkness-In dark prisons or dungeons.

title: Psalms 107:12
text: V. 12. Heart-The pride and obstinacy of their hearts. Fell-They fell into hopeless miseries.

title: Psalms 107:17
text: V. 17. Afflicted-With sickness.

title: Psalms 107:20
text: V. 20. Word-His command, or blessing.

title: Psalms 107:32
text: V. 32. Exalt him-In public assemblies, and before all persons, as they have opportunity.  Elders-The magistrates or rulers; let them not be ashamed nor afraid to speak of God's wonderful works, before the greatest of men.

title: Psalms 107:33
text: V. 33. Rivers-Those grounds which are well watered, and therefore fruitful.  And so the water-springs, here, and the standing water, ver. Psalms 107:35  are taken. Into-Into a dry ground, which is like a parched and barren wilderness.

title: Psalms 107:34
text: V. 34. For-He doth not inflict these judgments without cause, but for the punishment of sin in some, and the prevention of it in others.

title: Psalms 107:35
text: V. 35. Water-Into a well-watered and fruitful land.

title: Psalms 107:36
text: V. 36. Hungry-Poor people who could not provide for themselves.

title: Psalms 107:39
text: V. 39. They-These men, who when they are exalted by God, grow insolent and secure.  Low-By God's just judgment.

title: Psalms 107:40
text: V. 40. Contempt-Renders them despicable.  Wander-Banishes them from their own courts and kingdoms, and forces them to flee into desolate wildernesses for shelter.

title: Psalms 108:1
text:
PSALM CVIII. 
 
  The five first verses of this psalm are taken out of psalm 57,   the rest out of psalm 60.   David thanks God for personal mercies, ver. 1-5.   Prays for national mercies, ver. 6-13.   A song or psalm of David. 
 
  V. 1. Glory-With my tongue.

title: Psalms 109:1
text:
PSALM CIX. 
 
  David complains of his enemies and appeals to God, ver. 1-5.   Foretells their destruction, ver. 6-20.   Prays that God would succour him in his low condition, ver. 21-29.   Concludes with a joyful hope of deliverance, ver. 30, 31   To the chief musician, A psalm of David. 
 
  V. 1. God-The author and matter of all my praises.

title: Psalms 109:4
text: V. 4. Adversaries-They requite my love with enmity, as it is explained ver. Psalms 109:5 .

title: Psalms 109:6
text: V. 6. A wicked man-Who will rule him with rigour and cruelty. Satan-To accuse him; for this was the place and posture of accusers in the Jewish courts.

title: Psalms 109:7
text: V. 7. Sin-Because it is not from his heart.

title: Psalms 109:10
text: V. 10. Desolate places-Into which they are fled for fear and shame.

title: Psalms 109:11
text: V. 11. Catch-Heb. ensnare, take away not only by oppression but also by cunning artificers.  Stranger-Who hath no right to his goods.

title: Psalms 109:17
text: V. 17. Delighted not-In desiring and promoting the welfare of others.

title: Psalms 109:18
text: V. 18. Garment-Which a man wears constantly.  Like water-Water in the cavity of the belly, between the bowels, is almost certain death. And oil soaking into any of the bones, will soon utterly destroy it.

title: Psalms 109:20
text: V. 20. That speak evil against my soul-With design to take away my life.

title: Psalms 109:21
text: V. 21. Is good-Above the mercy of all the creatures.

title: Psalms 109:23
text: V. 23. When-Towards the evening, when the sun is setting. The locust-Which is easily driven away with every wind.

title: Psalms 110:1
text:
PSALM CX. 
 
  That this psalm belongs to the Messiah, is abundantly evident both from   the express testimony of the New Testament,    Acts 2:34 I Corinthians 15:25 Hebrews 1:13 Hebrews 10:13 .   and from the consent of the ancient Hebrew doctors.  Of him, it is   directly and immediately to be understood; the spirit of God wisely so   ordering this matter, that it might be a convincing testimony against   the unbelieving Jews, concerning the true Messiah, and concerning   the nature and quality of his kingdom.   His prophetic office, ver. 2.   His priestly office, ver. 4,   His kingly office, ver. 1, 3, 5, 6.   His states of humiliation and exaltation, ver. 7.   A psalm of David. 
 
  V. 1. The Lord-God the father.  Said-Decreed it from eternity, and in due time published this decree, and actually executed it; which he did when he raised up Christ from the dead, and brought him into his heavenly mansion.  Unto-Unto his son the Messiah, whom David designedly calls his Lord, to admonish the whole church, that although he was his son according to his human nature, yet he had an higher nature, and was also his Lord, as being God blessed for ever, and consequently Lord of all things.  The Hebrew word Adon is one of God's titles, signifying his power and authority over all things, and therefore is most fitly given to the Messiah, to whom God hath delegated all his power  Matthew 28:18 . Sit-Now take thy rest and the possession of that sovereign kingdom and glory, which by right belongeth to thee; do thou rule with me with equal power and majesty, as thou art God; and with an authority and honour far above all creatures, as thou art man.  Make-By my almighty power communicated to thee as God by eternal generation, and vouchsafed to thee as mediator.  Enemies-All ungodly men, sin and death, and the devil. Footstool-Thy slaves and vassals.

title: Psalms 110:2
text: V. 2. The rod-Thy strong or powerful rod, and the rod is put for his scepter, or kingly power: but as the kingdom of Christ is not carnal, but spiritual, so this scepter is nothing else but his word. Zion-From Jerusalem.

title: Psalms 110:3
text: V. 3. People-Thy subjects, shall offer thee as their king and Lord, not oxen or sheep, but themselves, their souls and bodies, as living sacrifices, and as freewill-offerings, giving up themselves to the Lord,  II Corinthians 8:5 , to live to him, and to die for him. The day-When thou shalt take into thy hands the rod of thy strength, and set up thy kingdom in the world.  In the beauties-Adorned with the beautiful and glorious robes of righteousness and true holiness. The dew-That is, thy offspring (the members of the Christian church) shall be more numerous than the drops of the morning dew.

title: Psalms 110:4
text: V. 4. Sworn-That this priesthood might be made sure and irrevocable.

title: Psalms 110:5
text: V. 5. The Lord-God the son; the Lord, who is at thy right-hand. Strike-Shall destroy all those kings who are obstinate enemies to him.

title: Psalms 110:6
text: V. 6. Judge-Condemn and punish them.  The places-Or, the place of battle.  Dead bodies-Of his enemies.  Heads-All those princes who oppose him.  But this and the like passages are not to be understood grossly, but spiritually, according to the nature of Christ's kingdom.

title: Psalms 110:7
text: V. 7. Drink-He shall have a large portion of afflictions, while he is in the way or course of his life, before he comes to that honour of sitting at his father's right-hand.  Waters in scripture frequently signify sufferings.  To drink of them, signifies to feel or bear them. Therefore-He shall be exalted to great glory and felicity.

title: Psalms 111:1
text:
PSALM CXI. 
 
  This and several of the following psalms seem to have been wrote for   the service of the church in their solemn feasts.  It is composed   alphabetically, each sentence beginning with a several letter of the   Hebrew alphabet.   The psalmist here praises God for his works, ver. 1-9.   Recommends the fear of God, ver. 10.

title: Psalms 111:2
text: V. 2. Sought-Diligently meditated upon.

title: Psalms 111:3
text: V. 3. Work-Either all his works, or that eminent branch of those works, his providence towards his people.  Righteousness-His justice or faithfulness in performing his word.

title: Psalms 111:4
text: V. 4. Remembered-By their own nature, and the lasting benefits flowing from them, which are such as cannot easily be forgotten.

title: Psalms 111:5
text: V. 5. Meat-All necessary provisions for their being and well-being.

title: Psalms 111:7
text: V. 7. The works-All that he doth on the behalf of his people, or against their enemies.  Truth-Are exactly agreeable to his promises, and to justice.  Commandments-His laws given to the Israelites, especially the moral law.  Sure-Constant and unchangeable.

title: Psalms 111:8
text: V. 8. Done-Constituted or ordered.

title: Psalms 111:9
text: V. 9. Redemption-The deliverance out of Egypt, which was a type of that higher redemption by Christ.  Commanded-Appointed, or established firmly by his power and authority.  For ever-Through all successive generations of his people to the end of the world.  Reverend-Terrible to his enemies, venerable in his peoples eyes, and holy in all his dealings with all men.

title: Psalms 111:10
text: V. 10. The fear-True religion.  Beginning-Is the only foundation of, and introduction to, true wisdom.

title: Psalms 112:1
text:
PSALM CXII. 
 
  This also is an alphabetical psalm.   We have here the character and blessedness of the righteous, ver. 1-9.   The iniquity of the wicked, ver. 10.

title: Psalms 112:2
text: V. 2. Generation-The posterity.

title: Psalms 112:3
text: V. 3. Righteousness-The fruit or reward of his righteousness, which is God's blessing upon his estate.

title: Psalms 112:4
text: V. 4. Darkness-In the troubles and calamities of life. He-The upright man.

title: Psalms 112:5
text: V. 5. Lendeth-Gives freely to some, and lends to others according to the variety of their conditions.  Affairs-His domestick affairs. Discretion-Not getting his estate unjustly, nor casting it away prodigally, nor yet withholding it from such as need it.

title: Psalms 112:6
text: V. 6. Moved-Though he may for a season be afflicted, yet he shall not be eternally destroyed.

title: Psalms 112:7
text: V. 7. Evil tidings-At the report of approaching calamities.

title: Psalms 112:9
text: V. 9. Dispersed-His goods, freely and liberally. Righteousness-His liberality, or the reward of it. Ever-What he gives is not lost, but indeed is the only part of his estate, which will abide with him to all eternity.

title: Psalms 112:10
text: V. 10. The desire-Either of the misery of good men; or of his own constant prosperity.

title: Psalms 113:1
text:
PSALM CXIII. 
 
  We are here exhorted to praise God, ver. 1-3.   Particularly for his glory and greatness, ver. 4, 5   And for his grace and goodness, ver. 6-9.

title: Psalms 113:6
text: V. 6. Humbleth-Who is so high, that it is a wonderful condescention in him to take any notice of his heavenly host, and much more of sinful and miserable men upon earth.

title: Psalms 113:8
text: V. 8. Princes-As he did Joseph, David, and others. His people-Who in God's account are far more honourable than the princes of Heathen nations.

title: Psalms 114:1
text:
PSALM CXIV. 
 
  This and the four following psalms, the Jews were wont to sing at   the close of the paschal supper.   It is a solemn commemoration of God's delivering Israel, giving them   the law, and water out of the rock, ver. 1-8.

title: Psalms 114:2
text: V. 2. Judah-Or Israel, one tribe being put for all. Judah he mentions as the chief of all the tribes.

title: Psalms 114:4
text: V. 4. The mountains-Horeb and Sinai, two tops of one mountain, and other neighbouring mountains.

title: Psalms 114:7
text: V. 7. Tremble-The mountains did more than what was fit at the appearance of the great God.

title: Psalms 115:1
text:
PSALM CXV. 
 
  We are to give glory to God, not to ourselves or idols, ver. 1-8.   By trusting in his promise and blessing, ver. 9-15.   And by praising him, ver. 16-18.

title: Psalms 115:8
text: V. 8. Are like them-As void of all sense or reason as their images.

title: Psalms 115:9
text: V. 9. Their-Who trust in him.

title: Psalms 115:10
text: V. 10. Aaron-You priests and Levites.

title: Psalms 115:11
text: V. 11. Ye that fear-All of you who worship the true God, not only Israelites, but even Gentile proselytes.

title: Psalms 115:12
text: V. 12. Mindful-In our former straits, and therefore we trust he will still bless us.

title: Psalms 115:13
text: V. 13. Both small-Of whatsoever quality, high and low, rich and poor.

title: Psalms 115:16
text: V. 16. The Lord's-In a peculiar manner, where he dwelleth in that light and glory, to which no man can approach.  Given-As the foregoing verse declares, that God was the creator of heaven and earth, so this asserts that he is also their Lord and governor to dispose of all men and things as he pleases.

title: Psalms 115:17
text: V. 17. Silence-Into the place of silence, the grave.

title: Psalms 116:1
text:
PSALM  CXVI. 
 
  This psalm is a solemn thanksgiving to God.   Wherein the psalmist professes his love to God, for delivering him out   of great straits and dangers, ver. 1-8.   Prays for his future protection, and promises to praise him, and to   walk holy before him, 9-19.

title: Psalms 116:3
text: V. 3. The sorrows-Dangerous and deadly calamities.   Pains-Such agonies and horrors, as dying persons use to feel.

title: Psalms 116:7
text: V.7. Rest-Unto a chearful confidence in God.

title: Psalms 117:1
text:
PSALM CXVII. 
 
  An exhortation to all nations to praise God for his mercy and truth,   ver. 1, 2.

title: Psalms 118:1
text:
PSALM CXVIII. 
 
  The form of this psalm seems to be dramatical, and several parts of it   are spoken in the name of several persons; as it is in the book of the   Song of Solomon, and in one part of Ecclesiastes.   David speaks in his own name from the beginning to ver. 22, from   thence to ver. 25, in the name of the people; and thence to ver. 28,   in the name of the priests; and then concludes in his own name.   He calls upon all about him to praise God, ver. 1-4.   Encourages himself and others to trust in God, from the experience   he had had of his power and mercy, ver. 5-18.   He gives thanks for his advancement to the throne, as it was a figure   of the exaltation of Christ, ver. 19-23.   The people, the priests, and the psalmist himself triumph in the   prospect of the Redeemer's kingdom, ver. 24-29.

title: Psalms 118:10
text: V. 10. Nations-The neighbouring nations, Philistines, Syrians, Ammonites, Moabites, who were stirred up, by the overthrows which David had given some of them, by their jealousy at his growing greatness, and by their hatred against the true religion.

title: Psalms 118:11
text: V. 11. Yea-The repetition implies their frequency and fervency in this action.

title: Psalms 118:12
text: V. 12. Bees-In great numbers.  Thorns-Which burns fiercely, but quickly spends itself.

title: Psalms 118:13
text: V. 13. Thou-O mine enemy.  The singular word is here put collectively for all his enemies.

title: Psalms 118:14
text: V. 14. Salvation-My Saviour.

title: Psalms 118:15
text: V. 15. Doth valiantly-These are the words of that song of praise now mentioned.

title: Psalms 118:16
text: V. 16. Exalted-Hath appeared evidently, and wrought powerfully and gloriously.

title: Psalms 118:19
text: V. 19. Open-O ye porters, appointed by God for this work. The gates-Of the Lord's tabernacle: where the rule of righteousness was kept and taught, and the sacrifices of righteousness were offered.

title: Psalms 118:20
text: V. 20. The righteous-As David was a type of Christ and the temple of heaven, so this place hath a farther prospect than David, and relates to Christ's ascending into heaven, and opening the gates of that blessed temple, both for himself and for all believers.

title: Psalms 118:22
text: V. 22. The builders-The commonwealth of Israel and the church of God are here and elsewhere compared to a building, wherein, as the people are the stones, so the princes and rulers are the builders. And as these master-builders rejected David, so their successors rejected Christ.  Head stone-The chief stone in the whole building, by which the several parts of the building are upheld and firmly united together.  Thus David united all the tribes and families of Israel: and thus Christ united Jews and Gentiles together. And therefore this place is justly expounded of Christ,  Mark 12:10 Acts 4:11 Romans 9:32 Ephesians 2:20 . And to him the words agree more properly than to David.

title: Psalms 118:24
text: V. 24. Made-Or sanctified as a season never to be forgotten.

title: Psalms 118:25
text: V. 25. We-These seem to be the words of the Levites, to whom he spake ver. Psalms 118:19 .

title: Psalms 118:26
text: V. 26. Blessed-We pray that God would bless his person and government. Cometh-To the throne; or from his Father into the world: who is known by the name of him that cometh or was to come, and of whom this very word is used,  Genesis 49:10 Isaiah 35:4 . Name-By commission from him.  We-We who are the Lord's ministers attending upon him in his house, and appointed to bless in his name,  Numbers 6:23 Deuteronomy 10:8 .  So these are the words of the priests.

title: Psalms 118:27
text: V. 27. The Lord-Or, The mighty God, as this name of God signifies, and as he shewed himself to be by this, his wonderful work.   Who-Who hath scattered our dark clouds, and put us into a state of peace, and safety, and happiness.  The horns-These are supposed to be made for this very use, that the beasts should be bound and killed there. These three last verses are David's words.

title: Psalms 119:1
text:
PSALM CXIX. 
 
  Because this psalm was very large, and the matter of it of the greatest   importance, the psalmist thought fit to divide it into two and twenty   several parts, according to the number of the Hebrew letters, that   he might both prevent tediousness, and fix it in the memory.  Each part   consists of eight verses.  All the verses of the first part beginning   with Aleph, all the verses of the second with Beth, and so on.   It is observable, that the word of God is here called by the names of   law, statutes, precepts or commandments, judgments, ordinances,   righteousness, testimonies, way and word.  By which variety, he   designed to express the nature and perfection of God's word.  It is   called his word, as revealed by him to us; his way, as   prescribed by him for us to walk in; his law, as binding us to   obedience; his statutes, as declaring his authority of giving us   laws; his precepts as directing our duty; his ordinances, as   ordained by him; his righteousness, as exactly agreeable to God's   righteous nature and will; his judgments, as proceeding from the   great judge of the world, and being his judicial sentence to which all   men must submit; and his testimonies, as it contains the witness of   God's will, and of man's duty.  And there is but one of these one   hundred and seventy six verses, in which one or other of these titles   is not found.  The general scope and design of this psalm is, to   magnify the law and make it honourable: to shew the excellency and   usefulness of divine revelation, and recommend it to us, by the   psalmist's own example, who speaks by experience of the benefits of it,   for which he praises God, and earnestly prays for the continuance of   God's grace, to direct and quicken him in his way.

title: Psalms 119:6
text: V. 6. Respect-A due respect, which implies hearty affection, diligent study, and constant practice.  To all-So as not to allow myself in any known sin, or in the neglect of any known duty.

title: Psalms 119:7
text: V. 7. When-When by thy good spirit I shall he more fitly instructed in the meaning of thy word.

title: Psalms 119:8
text: V. 8. Forsake me not-For then I shall fall into the foulest sins.

title: Psalms 119:9
text: V. 9. A young man-Or, any man.  But he names the young man, because such are commonly void of wisdom and experience, and exposed to many and great temptations.  Cleanse-Purge himself from all filthiness of flesh and spirit.

title: Psalms 119:11
text: V. 11. Hid-I have laid it up in my mind like a choice treasure, to be ready upon all occasions to counsel, quicken or caution me.

title: Psalms 119:17
text: V. 17. Live-Safely and comfortably.

title: Psalms 119:18
text: V. 18. Open-Enlighten my mind by the light of thy Holy Spirit, and dispel all ignorance and error.  Behold-Those great and marvellous depths of Divine wisdom and goodness, and those profound mysteries of Christ, and God's grace to mankind, and of that everlasting state, which are not to be known but by Divine illumination.

title: Psalms 119:19
text: V. 19. A stranger-I am not here as in my home, but as a pilgrim travelling homeward in a strange land.  Commandments-Which are my chief support and guide in my pilgrimage.

title: Psalms 119:20
text: V. 20. Breaketh-Faints, as it frequently does, when a thing vehemently desired is delayed.  Judgments-To a more sound knowledge and serious practice of them.

title: Psalms 119:21
text: V. 21. The proud-Obstinate and presumptuous sinners, who sin with an high hand.  Err-Or, wander, knowingly or wilfully.

title: Psalms 119:25
text: V. 25. The dust-I am in danger of present death: I am like one laid in the grave.  Quicken-Preserve my life, or raise me out of the dust. Word-According to thy promise.

title: Psalms 119:26
text: V. 26. My ways-My sins; and all my cares, and fears, and troubles.

title: Psalms 119:27
text: V. 27. Understand-More throughly.

title: Psalms 119:28
text: V. 28. Melteth-Like wax before the fire.

title: Psalms 119:29
text: V. 29. Grant me-Vouchsafe me an accurate knowledge of thy word, and let me govern myself by it in all things.

title: Psalms 119:30
text: V. 30. Laid-Or, set before me as a mark to aim at; as a rule to direct me.

title: Psalms 119:32
text: V. 32. Run-I will obey thy precepts with all readiness, fervency, and diligence.  Enlarge-When thou shalt replenish my heart with wisdom, and love to thee and thy law.

title: Psalms 119:36
text: V. 36. Covetousness-He mentions this in particular, because it is most opposite to God's testimonies, and does most commonly hinder men from receiving his word, and from profiting by it: and because it is most pernicious, as being the root of all evil.

title: Psalms 119:37
text: V. 37. Vanity-The vain things of this present world, such as riches, honours, pleasures: from beholding them, with desire or affection. Quicken-Make me lively, vigorous and fervent in thy service.

title: Psalms 119:38
text: V. 38. Stablish-Confirm and perform thy promises.

title: Psalms 119:39
text: V. 39. I fear-For my instability in thy ways; which in respect to my own weakness, I have great cause to fear.

title: Psalms 119:40
text: V. 40. Longed-After a more solid knowledge and constant performance of them.  In-According to thy faithfulness.

title: Psalms 119:43
text: V. 43. Take not-Do not deal so with me, that I shall be ashamed to mention thy word.  Judgments-In thy word.

title: Psalms 119:45
text: V. 45. At liberty-Enjoy great freedom and comfort in thy ways.

title: Psalms 119:48
text: V. 48. Lift up-To receive and embrace thy precepts and promises.

title: Psalms 119:49
text: V. 49. Thy word-Thy promises.

title: Psalms 119:52
text: V. 52. Judgments-Thy ancient dispensations to the children of men in punishing the ungodly.

title: Psalms 119:53
text: V. 53. Horror-A mixed passion, made up of abhorrence of their sins, and dread and sorrow at the consideration of the judgments of God coming upon them.

title: Psalms 119:54
text: V. 54. The house-In this world, wherein I am a stranger and pilgrim, as all my fathers were.

title: Psalms 119:55
text: V. 55. Thy name-Thy holy nature and attributes, thy blessed word, and thy wonderful works.  In the night-When darkness causes fear in others, I took pleasure in remembering thee; and when others gave themselves up to sleep, my thoughts and affections were working towards thee.

title: Psalms 119:56
text: V. 56. This-This comfortable remembrance.

title: Psalms 119:57
text: V. 57. Said-I have professed and owned it.

title: Psalms 119:59
text: V. 59. Thought-I seriously considered both my former courses, and my duty in all my future actions.

title: Psalms 119:61
text: V. 61. Robbed-Done me many injuries, for my respect to thy law.

title: Psalms 119:66
text: V. 66. Judgment-Whereby I may rightly discern between truth and falsehood.  Knowledge-A spiritual experimental knowledge.

title: Psalms 119:70
text: V. 70. Fat-They are stupid and insensible.

title: Psalms 119:74
text: V. 74. Glad-For the encouragement they have by my example to trust in God.  See me-Alive and in safety.  Word-In thy promise, and have not been disappointed of my hope.

title: Psalms 119:75
text: V. 75. Judgments-Thy corrections.  Of faithfulness-In pursuance of thy promises, and in order to my good.

title: Psalms 119:79
text: V. 79. Known-Loved and practised them.

title: Psalms 119:80
text: V. 80. Sound-That I may love and obey them sincerely, constantly, and universally.

title: Psalms 119:81
text: V. 81. Fainteth-With long desire and earnest expectation.

title: Psalms 119:83
text: V. 83. Bottle-A leathern bottle.  My natural moisture is dryed and burnt up.

title: Psalms 119:84
text: V. 84. The days-The days of my life.  I have but a little while to live; give me some respite before I die.

title: Psalms 119:85
text: V. 85. Who-Who have no respect to thy law.

title: Psalms 119:86
text: V. 86. Faithful-Just and true.

title: Psalms 119:89
text: V. 89. In heaven-With thee in thy heavenly habitation.

title: Psalms 119:91
text: V. 91. They-The heaven and the earth.  Ordinances-As thou hast appointed.  For-All things are subject to thy power and pleasure.

title: Psalms 119:96
text: V. 96. Perfection-Of the greatest and most perfect enjoyments in this world.  Commandment-Thy word; one part of it being put for the whole. Broad-Or, large, both for extent, and for continuance: it is useful to all persons: it is of everlasting truth and efficacy; it will never deceive those who trust to it, as all worldly things will, but will make men happy both here and for ever.

title: Psalms 119:100
text: V. 100. Because-The practice of religion is the best way to understand it.

title: Psalms 119:102
text: V. 102. Taught me-By thy blessed spirit, illuminating my mind, and working upon my heart.

title: Psalms 119:108
text: V. 108. Offerings-The sacrifices of prayer and praise.

title: Psalms 119:109
text: V. 109. Is-Exposed to perpetual danger.

title: Psalms 119:118
text: V. 118. Deceit-Their deceitful devices, shall bring that destruction upon themselves which they design for others.

title: Psalms 119:121
text: V. 121. Judgment, &c.-Just judgment.

title: Psalms 119:122
text: V. 122. Surety-Do thou undertake and plead my cause.

title: Psalms 119:123
text: V. 123. The word-For the performance of thy faithful or merciful promise.

title: Psalms 119:126
text: V. 126. To work-To put forth thy power for the restraint of evil-doers. They-The wicked.  Made void-Or, abrogated thy law, have openly cast off its authority.

title: Psalms 119:127
text: V. 127. Therefore-Because the general apostacy of others makes this duty more necessary.

title: Psalms 119:129
text: V. 129. Wonderful-In regard of the deep mysteries, the most excellent directions, and the exceeding great and precious promises of God contained in them.

title: Psalms 119:131
text: V. 131. Panted-I thirst after thy precepts, and pursue them eagerly.

title: Psalms 119:133
text: V. 133. Steps-My motions and actions.

title: Psalms 119:136
text: V. 136. Rivers-Plentiful tears, witness of my deep sorrow for God's dishonour, and for the miseries which sinners bring upon themselves.

title: Psalms 119:140
text: V. 140. Pure-Without the least mixture of falsehood.

title: Psalms 119:142
text: V. 142. Everlasting-The same in all ages and places.

title: Psalms 119:143
text: V. 143. Trouble-Outward troubles and anguish of spirit.

title: Psalms 119:148
text: V. 148. Watches-The middle watch, which was set in the middle of the night; and the morning watch, which was set some hours before the dawning of the day.

title: Psalms 119:149
text: V. 149. Judgment-According to thy word.

title: Psalms 119:150
text: V. 150. Nigh-To me, they are at hand and ready to seize upon me. Are far-They cast away from them all thoughts of thy law.

title: Psalms 119:152
text: V. 152. Of old-By long experience.  Founded-Thou hast established them upon everlasting foundations.

title: Psalms 119:160
text: V. 160. The beginning-From the beginning of the world.

title: Psalms 119:161
text: V. 161. But-But I feared thine offence and displeasure more than their wrath.

title: Psalms 119:164
text: V. 164. Seven times-Many times; a certain number being put for an uncertain.

title: Psalms 119:165
text: V. 165. Offend-Heb. they shall have no stumbling-block, at which they shall stumble and fall into mischief.

title: Psalms 119:175
text: V. 175. Judgments-Thy word or testimonies, which are the only ground of my hope in thy help.

title: Psalms 120:1
text:
PSALM CXX. 
 
  David prays against lying tongues, and denounces judgment against them,   ver. 1-4.   Complains of his wicked and unpeaceable neighbours, ver. 5-7.   A song of degrees. 
 
Title of the psalm.  Of degrees-Or, of accents, as the word properly signifies.  This title is given to this and the fourteen following psalms, probably because they were sung upon the fifteen degrees, steps, or stairs of the temple, which the Jewish writers mention.

title: Psalms 120:4
text: V. 4. Arrows-The wrath and vengeance of the mighty God, which in scripture is often compared to arrows, and here to coals of juniper, which burn very fiercely and retain their heat for a long time.

title: Psalms 120:5
text: V. 5. Mesech-Mesech and Kedar are two sorts of people often mentioned in scripture, and reckoned amongst the barbarous nations. But their names are here to be understood metaphorically.  And so he explains himself in the next verse.

title: Psalms 121:1
text:
PSALM CXXI. 
 
  David assures himself of help from God, ver. 1, 2.   He assures others of it, ver. 3-8.   A song of degrees. 
 
  V. 1. Hills-To Sion and Moriah, which are called the holy mountains.

title: Psalms 121:5
text: V. 5. Shade-To keep thee from the burning heat of the sun.

title: Psalms 121:6
text: V. 6. Smite-With excessive heat.  Moon-With that cold and moisture which come into the air by it.  Intemperate heats and colds are the springs of many diseases.

title: Psalms 122:1
text:
PSALM CXXII. 
 
  This psalm seems to have been wrote for the use of the people, when   they came to Jerusalem at the three solemn feasts.   David here shews the joy with which they were to go up to Jerusalem,   ver. 1, 2.   The esteem they were to have of it, ver. 3-5.   The prayers they were to make for its welfare, ver, 6-9.   A song of degrees of David.

title: Psalms 122:4
text: V. 4. The tribes-Whom God has chosen to be his people.  Unto-Unto the ark, called the testimony, because of the tables of the covenant laid up in it, which are called God's testimony, and the tables of the testimony.  And this is called the testimony of, or to Israel, because it was given by God to them.  Give thanks-To worship God; this one eminent part thereof being put for all the rest.

title: Psalms 122:5
text: V. 5. Judgment-The supreme courts of justice for ecclesiastical and civil affairs.  Thrones-The royal throne allotted by God to David and to his posterity, and the inferior seats of justice under his authority.

title: Psalms 123:1
text:
PSALM CXXIII. 
 
  The psalmist expresses and prays for deliverance from trouble,   ver. 1-4.   A song of degrees.

title: Psalms 123:2
text: V. 2. Look-For supply of their wants, and for help and defence against their oppressors.  Until-Until he help and save us.

title: Psalms 124:1
text:
PSALM CXXIV. 
 
  David describes the danger he and his people had been in, ver. 1-5.   Blesses God for delivering them, ver. 6-8.   A song of degrees of David.

title: Psalms 124:5
text: V. 5. The proud-Our enemies, compared to proud waters, for their great multitude and swelling rage.

title: Psalms 125:1
text:
PSALM CXXV. 
 
  The safety of them that trust in God, and the fate of the wicked,   ver. 1-5.   A song of degrees.

title: Psalms 125:3
text: V. 3. The rod-Their power and authority.  Not rest-Not continue long.  The lot-Upon the habitations and persons of good men. Lest-Lest they should be driven to indirect courses to relieve themselves.

title: Psalms 125:5
text: V. 5. Lead them-Unto sinful courses. Israel-Upon the true Israel of God.

title: Psalms 126:1
text:
PSALM CXXVI. 
 
  This psalm was probably composed by Ezra, at the return of Israel   from Babylon.  Those who are returned, are called upon to be   thankful; those who still remain there, are prayed for and encouraged,   ver. 1-6.   A song of degrees. 
 
  V. 1. Turned-Brought the captive Israelites out of Babylon into their own land.  Dream-We were so surprized and astonished.

title: Psalms 126:4
text: V. 4. Turn-As thou hast brought us home, bring also the rest of our brethren.  As-As thou art pleased sometimes to send floods of water into dry and barren grounds, such as the southern parts of Canaan were.

title: Psalms 127:1
text:
PSALM CXXVII. 
 
  We must trust in God for success in all enterprizes, ver. 1, 2.   And for children, ver. 3-5.   A song of degrees of Solomon. 
 
  V. 1. Build-Assist and bless those that build it.

title: Psalms 127:2
text: V. 2. You-Builders, or watchmen.  To sit-To use constant and unwearied diligence.  So-By his blessing.  Giveth-Freely, without that immoderate toiling, wherewith others pursue it.

title: Psalms 127:3
text: V. 3. Children-The chief of these blessings.  Heritage-Only from God's blessing, even as an inheritance is not the fruit of a man's own labour, but the gift of God.

title: Psalms 127:4
text: V. 4. Youth-These he prefers before other children, because they live longest with their parents, and to their comfort and support, whereas children born in old age seldom come to maturity before their parents death.

title: Psalms 127:5
text: V. 5. Full-Who hath a numerous issue.  Shall speak-They shall courageously plead their cause in courts of judicature, not fearing to be crushed by the might of their adversaries.

title: Psalms 128:1
text:
PSALM CXXVIII. 
 
  The happiness of them that fear God, ver. 1-6.   A song of degrees.

title: Psalms 128:3
text: V. 3. Olive-plants-Numerous, growing and flourishing.

title: Psalms 129:1
text:
PSALM CXXIX. 
 
  The people of God commemorate their deliverance out of sore   afflictions, ver. 1-4.   The destruction of their enemies, ver. 5-8.   A song of degrees. 
 
  V. 1. From my youth-From the time that I was a people.

title: Psalms 129:4
text: V. 4. Righteous-Faithful or merciful.  The cords-Wherewith the plow was drawn.  By these cords he understands all their plots and endeavours.

title: Psalms 129:6
text: V. 6. House-tops-Which there were flat.  Which-Having no deep root, never comes to maturity.  And so all their designs shall be abortive.

title: Psalms 129:8
text: V. 8. The blessing-Which was an usual salutation given by passengers to reapers: so the meaning is, it never continues 'till the harvest comes.

title: Psalms 130:1
text:
PSALM CXXX. 
 
  The psalmist confessing his sins, expresses his hope in God, ver. 1-6.   And exhorts Israel to hope in him, ver.7, 8.   A song of degrees.

title: Psalms 130:3
text: V. 3. Mark-Observe them accurately and punish them as they deserve. Stand-At thy tribunal.

title: Psalms 130:4
text: V. 4. Forgiveness-Thou art able and ready to forgive repenting sinners. Feared-Not with a slavish, but with a childlike fear.  This mercy of thine is the foundation of all religion, without which men would desperately proceed in their impious courses.

title: Psalms 130:5
text: V. 5. I wait-That he would pardon my sins.

title: Psalms 130:6
text: V. 6. They-Whether soldiers that keep the night-watches in an army, or the priests or Levites who did so in the temple.

title: Psalms 130:7
text: V. 7. Israel-Every true Israelite.  Plenteous-Abundantly sufficient for all persons who accept it upon God's terms.

title: Psalms 131:1
text:
PSALM CXXXI. 
 
  David testifies his humility, and exhorts Israel to trust in God,   ver. 1-3.   A song of degrees of David.

title: Psalms 131:2
text: V. 2. Surely-When my mind was provoked.  Weaned-Wholly depending upon God's providence, as the poor helpless infant, relies upon its mother for support.

title: Psalms 132:1
text:
PSALM CXXXII. 
 
  Probably this psalm was wrote by Solomon to be sung at the   dedication of the temple, of which he desires God would come and take   possession, ver. 8, 9, 10.   With these words he concluded his prayer,  II Chronicles 6:41 II Chronicles 6:42 .   He pleads David's piety towards God, ver. 1-7.   And God's promise to David, ver. 11-18.   A song of degrees. 
 
  V. 1. Afflictions-All his sufferings for thy sake.

title: Psalms 132:5
text: V. 5. Until-Until I have raised an house in which the ark may be put.

title: Psalms 132:6
text: V. 6. It-Of the ark.  Ephratah-In the tribe of Ephraim, which was called also Ephratah.  Found it-Afterwards we found it in Kirjath-jearim, which signifies a city of woods, in the territory whereof the ark was seated for twenty years.

title: Psalms 132:7
text: V. 7. Tabernacles-Into his temple.  Footstool-The ark, is often said to sit between the cherubim, which were above the ark.

title: Psalms 132:8
text: V. 8. Rest-Into thy resting place, the temple so called,  Isaiah 66:1 , where thou hast now a fixed habitation. The ark-The seat of thy powerful and glorious presence.

title: Psalms 132:10
text: V. 10. David's sake-In regard of thy promises vouchsafed to David. Turn not-Cast me not out of thy presence.  Of-Of me whom thou hast anointed to be king over thy people.

title: Psalms 132:16
text: V. 16. Salvation-With thy saving graces and blessings.

title: Psalms 132:17
text: V. 17. There-In Jerusalem.  To bud-His power and glory to flourish.  A lamp-A successor to continue for ever in his family, as this phrase is expounded  I Kings 11:36 I Kings 15:4 , and particularly one eminent and glorious light, namely, the Messiah.

title: Psalms 133:1
text:
PSALM CXXXIII. 
 
  The happiness of brotherly love, ver. 1-3.   A song of degrees of David.

title: Psalms 133:2
text: V. 2. Ointment-It is no less grateful and refreshing than that oil which was poured forth upon Aaron's head at the time of his consecration to the priestly office.  Skirts-Not to the lower skirt or bottom of his sacerdotal garment, but to the upper skirt of it, or the mouth of it, as the Hebrew word properly signifies.

title: Psalms 133:3
text: V. 3. Zion-It is as desirable as the dew which falls upon mount Hermon, nay, as desirable as that heavenly dew of God's ordinances and graces which he hath commanded to fall upon the mountains of Zion and Moriah, and others which are round about Jerusalem. There-Where brethren live in peace and unity.

title: Psalms 134:1
text:
PSALM CXXXIV. 
 
  In this psalm the priests or Levites who watched all night in the   temple, exhort one another, and pray for one another, ver. 1-3.   A song of degrees. 
 
  V. 1. Servant-Peculiarly so called, priests and Levites. Night-Not only by day, but also by night, when their watch was more necessary.  Stand-Serve or minister.

title: Psalms 134:3
text: V. 3. Thee-Thee whosoever thou art who dost faithfully perform the duty here commanded.

title: Psalms 135:1
text:
PSALM CXXXV. 
 
  An exhortation to praise God for his greatness and mighty works,   ver. 1-7.   For destroying his enemies, ver. 8-11.   For his mercy toward Israel, ver. 12-14.   The vanity of idols, ver. 15-18.   Another exhortation to praise God, ver. 19-20.

title: Psalms 135:2
text: V. 2. Ye-Ye priest and Levites.

title: Psalms 135:6
text: V. 6. Seas-In the visible seas, and in the invisible depths both of the earth and of the waters.

title: Psalms 135:7
text: V. 7. From-From all parts of the earth, from one end to another. Rain-An eminent instance of his good providence.

title: Psalms 135:14
text: V. 14. Judge-Will in due time plead the cause of his people. Repent-He will recall that severe sentence which for their sins he had passed upon them.

title: Psalms 136:1
text:
PSALM CXXXVI. 
 
  We must praise God as great and good in himself, ver. 1-3.   As the Creator of the world, ver. 4-9.   As Israel's God, ver. 10-22.   As our Redeemer, ver. 23, 24.   As God over all, ver. 25, 26.

title: Psalms 136:2
text: V. 2. The God of gods-Who is infinitely superior to all that are called gods, whether angels, or princes, or idols.

title: Psalms 136:22
text: V. 22. Israel-He speaks of all that people as of one man, because they were united together in one body in the worship of God.

title: Psalms 136:25
text: V. 25. Food-To all living creatures. For which God deserves great praises, which the psalmist teaches us to render to God for them, because those who are most concerned, either cannot, or do not perform this duty.

title: Psalms 137:1
text:
PSALM CXXXVII. 
 
  Probably this psalm was wrote toward the end of the Babylonish   captivity.  Herein the captives complain of the scoffs of their   enemies, yet remember Jerusalem, and foresee the downfall of   Babylon, ver. 1-9. 
 
  V. 1. Sat-The usual posture of mourners.

title: Psalms 137:2
text: V. 2. Harps-Harps are here put for all instruments of musick.

title: Psalms 137:3
text: V. 3. A song-Such songs as you used to sing in the temple of Zion.

title: Psalms 137:4
text: V. 4. The Lord's-Those songs which were appointed by God to be sung only in his service.

title: Psalms 137:6
text: V. 6. If-If I do not value Jerusalem's prosperity more than all other delights.

title: Psalms 137:7
text: V. 7. The day-In the time of its destruction.

title: Psalms 137:8
text: V. 8. Happy-As being God's instrument to vindicate his honour, and execute his just judgments.

title: Psalms 138:1
text:
PSALM CXXXVIII. 
 
  David praises God for his goodness, and foretells that other kings   will praise him, ver. 1-5.   He rejoices in hope of still greater blessings, ver. 6-8.   A psalm of David. 
 
  V. 1. The gods-Before kings and princes.

title: Psalms 138:2
text: V. 2. Temple-Where the ark was.  He was not permitted to enter into it. Magnified-For thou hast glorified thy word or promise unto me more than any other of thy glorious perfections.

title: Psalms 138:4
text: V. 4. The kings-A prophecy of the calling of the Gentiles. Hear-The gospel preached among then.

title: Psalms 138:5
text: V. 5. The ways-His wonderful counsel and gracious providences.

title: Psalms 138:8
text: V. 8. Perfect-Will finish the great work of my deliverance. Forsake not-Or, do not give over, the work of my salvation, which is thus far advanced, not by any human help, but by thy power and providence.

title: Psalms 139:1
text:
PSALM CXXXIX. 
 
  This psalm is, by many of the Jewish doctors, esteemed the most   excellent in the whole book.   The omniscience of God is here asserted, ver. 1-6.   Proved by two arguments; That he is every where present, ver. 7-12.   And that he made us, ver. 13-16.   This may fill us with pleasing admiration of God, ver. 17, 18.   With an holy hatred of sin, ver. 19-22.   And with an holy satisfaction in our own integrity, ver. 23, 24.   To the chief musician, A psalm of David.

title: Psalms 139:2
text: V. 2. Afar off-Thou knowest what my thoughts will be in such and such circumstances, long before I know it, yea from all eternity.

title: Psalms 139:3
text: V. 3. Compassest-Thou discernest every step I take.  It is a metaphor from soldiers besieging their enemies, and setting watches round about them.

title: Psalms 139:5
text: V. 5. Beset me-With thy all-seeing providence.  And laid-Thou keepest me, as it were with a strong hand, in thy sight and under thy power.

title: Psalms 139:6
text: V. 6. I cannot-Apprehend in what manner thou dost so presently know all things.

title: Psalms 139:8
text: V. 8. Hell-If I could hide myself in the lowest parts of the earth.

title: Psalms 139:9
text: V. 9. The wings-If I should flee from east to west: for the sea being the western border of Canaan, is often put for the west in scripture. And wings are poetically ascribed to the morning here, as they are elsewhere to the sun, and to the winds.

title: Psalms 139:16
text: V. 16. Imperfect-When I was first conceived.  Book-In thy counsel and providence, by which thou didst contrive and effect this great work, according to that model which thou hadst appointed.

title: Psalms 139:17
text: V. 17. Thoughts-Thy counsels on my behalf.  Thou didst not only form me at first, but ever since my conception and birth, thy thoughts have been employed for me.

title: Psalms 139:18
text: V. 18. Them-Thy wonderful counsels and works on my behalf come constantly into my mind.

title: Psalms 139:22
text: V. 22. Perfect hatred-See the difference between the Jewish and the Christian spirit!

title: Psalms 140:1
text:
PSALM CXL. 
 
  David prays and hopes for deliverance from his enemies, ver. 1-7.   Foretells their destruction, ver. 8-13.   To the chief musician, A psalm of David.

title: Psalms 140:3
text: V. 3. Tongues-Using words as sharp and piercing as the sting of a serpent.

title: Psalms 140:9
text: V. 9. Mischief-The mischief which they design against me, shall fall upon themselves.

title: Psalms 140:10
text: V. 10. Coals-Divine vengeance, which is compared to coals of fire.

title: Psalms 140:13
text: V. 13. Dwell-Shall constantly enjoy thy gracious and powerful presence.

title: Psalms 141:1
text:
PSALM CXLI. 
 
  David prays for acceptance and assistance, ver. 1-6.   For the deliverance of himself and friends, ver. 7-10.   A psalm of David.

title: Psalms 141:4
text: V. 4. Incline not-Suffer it not to be inclined.  Heart-Keep me not only from wicked speeches, but from all evil motions of my heart. Dainties-The pleasures or advantages which they gain by their wickedness.

title: Psalms 141:5
text: V. 5. Smite-By reproofs.  Break-Not hurt, but heal and greatly refresh me.  Calamities-In the calamities of those righteous persons who reproved him.  When they came into such calamities as those wherein he was involved he would pity them and pray for them.

title: Psalms 141:6
text: V. 6. Judges-The chief of mine enemies.  Overthrown-Or, cast down headlong by thine exemplary vengeance.  Hear-Hearken unto my counsels and offers which now they despise.

title: Psalms 141:7
text: V. 7. Our bones-Our case is almost as hopeless as of those who are dead, and whose bones are scattered in several places.

title: Psalms 142:1
text:
PSALM CXLII. 
 
  David complains to God and trusts in him, ver. 1-7   Maschil of David; A prayer when he was in the cave.

title: Psalms 142:3
text: V. 3. Knowest-So as to direct me to it.  My path-What paths I should chuse whereby I might escape.

title: Psalms 142:4
text: V. 4. Right-hand-The place where the patron or assistant used to stand.

title: Psalms 142:5
text: V. 5. Portion-Even in this life.

title: Psalms 142:7
text: V. 7. Prison-Set me at liberty.  Compass-Shall flock to me from all parts, to rejoice and bless God with me and for me.

title: Psalms 143:1
text:
PSALM CLXIII. 
 
  David complains and prays for pardon and help, ver. 1-12.   A psalm of David.

title: Psalms 143:2
text: V. 2. Justified-Upon terms of strict justice.

title: Psalms 143:3
text: V. 3. For-This is not a reason of what he last said, but an argument to enforce his petition delivered, ver. Psalms 143:1 . Soul-My life; nothing less will satisfy him.  Dead-I am in as hopeless a condition in the eye of man, as those that have lain long in the grave.

title: Psalms 143:5
text: V. 5. The days-What thou hast done for thy servants in former times.

title: Psalms 143:6
text: V. 6. As land-Thirsteth for rain.

title: Psalms 143:8
text: V. 8. Morning-Seasonably and speedily.

title: Psalms 144:1
text:
PSALM CXLIV. 
 
  David blesses God for his mercies, ver. 1-4.   Prays against his enemies, ver. 5-8.   Promises to praise him, ver.9-11.   The happiness of those who serve God, ver. 12-15.   A psalm of David.

title: Psalms 144:2
text: V. 2. Subdued-Who hath disposed my peoples hearts to receive and obey me as their king.

title: Psalms 144:5
text: V. 5. Come-To help me.  Smoke-As Sinai did at thy glorious appearance,  Exodus 19:18 .  This is a figurative and poetical description of God's coming to take vengeance upon his enemies.

title: Psalms 144:7
text: V. 7. Strange children-Either of the Heathen nations: or of the rebellious Israelites.

title: Psalms 144:8
text: V. 8. Vanity-Vain brags and threatenings which shall come to nothing. Falsehood-Deceiving themselves, by being unable to do what they designed; and others, by not giving them that help which they promised.

title: Psalms 144:12
text: V. 12. That-This mercy I beg not only for my own sake, but for the sake of thy people, that they may enjoy those blessings which thou hast promised them; and particularly, that our sons, who are the strength and hopes of a nation, may be like plants, flourishing and growing in height and strength, as plants do in their youth; for when they grow old, they wither and decay.  Cornerstone-Strong and beautiful.

title: Psalms 144:14
text: V. 14. Breaking in-Of enemies invading the land, or assaulting our cities, and making breaches in their walls.  Going out-Of our people, either out of the cities to fight with an invading enemy: or out of the land into captivity.

title: Psalms 145:1
text:
PSALM CXLV. 
 
  This also is an alphabetical psalm.   In it David praises God for his greatness, ver. 1-7.   For his goodness and everlasting kingdom, ver. 8-13.   For his providence, ver. 14-16.   For his mercy to his servants, ver. 17-21.   David's psalm of praise.

title: Psalms 145:14
text: V. 14. All-All that look up to him for help.

title: Psalms 145:15
text: V. 15. All-Of all living creatures.  Wait-Expect their supplies wholly from thy bounty.  Expectation is here figuratively ascribed to brute creatures.

title: Psalms 145:18
text: V. 18. Nigh-To answer their prayers.  In truth-With an upright heart.

title: Psalms 146:1
text:
PSALM CXLVI. 
 
  The psalmist praises God, and exhorts all to trust in him alone,   ver. 1-5.   Because of his power, faithfulness and everlasting kingdom, ver. 6-10.

title: Psalms 146:4
text: V. 4. That day-As soon as ever he is dead.  Thoughts-All his designs and endeavours either for himself or for others.

title: Psalms 146:6
text: V. 6. For ever-Both because he liveth for ever to fulfil his promises, and because he is eternally faithful.

title: Psalms 147:1
text:
PSALM CXXVII. 
 
  The psalmist praises God for his care over the church, ver. 1-14.   His government over all, ver. 15-18.   His giving his word to Israel, ver. 19, 20.

title: Psalms 147:4
text: V. 4. Calleth them-He exactly knows them as we do those whom we can call by name.

title: Psalms 147:9
text: V. 9. Ravens-Which he mentions because they were most contemptible, especially to the Jews, to whom they were unclean: and because they are not only neglected by men, but also forsaken by their dams as soon as ever they can fly, and so are wholly left to the care of Divine providence.

title: Psalms 147:10
text: V. 10. Delighteth not-As if he needed either the one or the other for the accomplishment of his designs.

title: Psalms 147:13
text: V. 13. Thy gates-Thy strength consists not in thy walls, and gates, and bars, but in his protection.

title: Psalms 147:14
text: V. 14. Borders-In all thy land, even to its utmost borders.

title: Psalms 147:15
text: V. 15. Commandment-Which is sufficient without any instruments to execute whatsoever pleaseth him.  Swiftly-The thing is done without delay.

title: Psalms 147:16
text: V. 16. Like wool-Not only in colour and shape, and softness, but also in use, keeping the fruits of the earth warm.  Ashes-In colour and smallness of parts, as also in its burning quality.

title: Psalms 147:17
text: V. 17. Ice-Great hail-stones, which are of an icy nature, and are cast forth out of the clouds, like morsels or fragments.

title: Psalms 148:1
text:
PSALM CXLVIII. 
 
  An exhortation to all creatures in heaven and earth, man especially,   to praise God, ver. 1-14.

title: Psalms 148:4
text: V. 4. Heavens of heavens-Ye highest heavens, the place of God's throne. Waters-Ye clouds which are above a part of the heavens.

title: Psalms 148:6
text: V. 6. Established-He hath made them constant and incorruptible, not changeable, as the things of the lower world.  A decree-Concerning their continuance.

title: Psalms 148:7
text: V. 7. Dragons-Either serpents, which hide in the deep caverns of the earth; or whales, and other sea-monsters, which dwell in the depths of the sea.

title: Psalms 148:8
text: V. 8. Fire-Lightnings and other fireworks of the air.  Vapour-Or, fumes: hot exhalations.  Fulfilling his word-Executing his commands, either for the comfort or punishment of the inhabitants of the earth.

title: Psalms 148:13
text: V. 13. Above-Above all the glories which are in earth and in heaven.

title: Psalms 148:14
text: V. 14. The horn-In scripture commonly denotes strength, victory, glory, and felicity.

title: Psalms 149:1
text:
PSALM CXLIX. 
 
  An exhortation to praise God for his love to his people, ver. 1-5.   And for enabling them to overcome their enemies, ver. 6-9.

title: Psalms 149:4
text: V. 4. The Lord-He rejoiceth over them to do them good. Beautify-Heb. adorn, make them amiable and honourable in the eyes of the world, who now hate and despise them. The meek-All true Israelites are such.

title: Psalms 149:5
text: V. 5. In glory-For the honour which God putteth upon them. Beds-By night as well as by day.

title: Psalms 149:7
text: V. 7. Vengeance-For all their cruelties and injuries towards God's people.  This was literally accomplished by David upon the Philistines, Ammonites, Syrians and other neighbouring nations.

title: Psalms 149:9
text: V. 9. Written-Appointed and declared in the holy scripture.

title: Psalms 150:1
text:
PSALM CL. 
 
  An exhortation to praise God with all sorts of musical instruments,   ver. 1-6. 
 
  V. 1. Sanctuary-In his temple.  The firmament-In heaven: there let the blessed angels praise him.

title: Psalms 150:6
text: V. 6. Also-Every living creature in heaven and in earth.

title: Proverbs 1:1
text:
NOTES                             ON                    The Book of PROVERBS 
 
  We have here a new way of writing, wherein Divine wisdom is taught us   in Proverbs or short sentences, which contain their whole design   within themselves, and are not connected with one another.  And these   Proverbs of Solomon are not merely a collection of the wise sayings   which had been formerly delivered, but were the dictates of the Spirit   of God in Solomon: so that it is God by Solomon that here speaks   to us.  I say, to us: for when Solomon speaks to his son, St. Paul   says, The exhortation speaketh to us, as unto children.  The nine   first chapters are as a preface exhorting us to the study and practice   of wisdom, and warning us against the things that would hinder it.   We have then the first volume of Solomon's Proverbs, chap. 10-24.   After that a second volume, chap. 25-29.   And then Agur's prophecy, chap. 30.   And Lemuel's, chap. 31.   The scope of all is, to direct us so to order our conversation, that we   may see the salvation of God. 
 
                        PROVERBS.                          CHAP. I. 
 
  The title of the book, shewing the general design of it, ver. 1-6.   The first principle of it recommended, ver. 7-9.   A caution against bad company, ver. 10-19.   Wisdom's reasonings with the sons of men, and the certain ruin of those   who will not hearken unto them, ver. 20-33.

title: Proverbs 1:2
text: V. 2. To know-Written to help men to know throughly and practically. Both human wisdom to conduct our affairs in this life, and Divine wisdom. Instruction-The instructions delivered either by God, or men, in order to the attainment of wisdom.  To perceive-Which teach a man true understanding.

title: Proverbs 1:3
text: V. 3. To receive-Willing to receive the counsels of others.  Such as makes men wise and prudent, and to teach just judgments or equity.

title: Proverbs 1:4
text: V. 4. Simple-Such as want wisdom.  Young man-Who wants both experience and self-government.

title: Proverbs 1:5
text: V. 5. Will hear-Is willing to learn.  Attain to-The art of governing himself or others.

title: Proverbs 1:7
text: V. 7. The fear-Reverence and obedience to God.  Beginning-The foundation without which all other knowledge is vain.  Fools-That is, wicked men, are so far from attaining true wisdom, that they despise it, and all the means of getting it.

title: Proverbs 1:8
text: V. 8. My son-He speaks to his scholars with paternal authority and affection.  Of thy mother-Those pious instructions, which thy mother instilled into thee in thy tender years.

title: Proverbs 1:17
text: V. 17. In vain-The fowler who spreads, his net in the sight of the bird looseth his labour.  But these, are more foolish than the silly birds, and though they are not ignorant of the mischief which these evil courses will bring upon themselves, yet they will not take warning.

title: Proverbs 1:18
text: V. 18. Their own blood-The destruction which they design to others, fall upon themselves.

title: Proverbs 1:19
text: V. 19. Greedy-That seeks gain by wicked practices.

title: Proverbs 1:20
text: V. 20. Wisdom-Having expressed the counsels of wicked men, he now declares the voice of wisdom.  By wisdom he understands the wisdom of God revealed to men in his word.  And this is said to cry with a loud voice, to intimate God's earnestness in inviting sinners to repentance. Abroad-Or, in the streets or open places.  Not in corners, but openly before all the world.

title: Proverbs 1:21
text: V. 21. Gates-Where magistrates sit in judgment, and people are assembled.  The city-Not only in the gate, but in every part of the city.

title: Proverbs 1:22
text: V. 22. Scoffers-That scoff at religion and contemn the word and faithful ministers of God.

title: Proverbs 1:23
text: V. 23. My words-By my spirit I will cause you to understand my word.

title: Proverbs 1:24
text: V. 24. Called-By my ministers, by my judgments, and by the motions of my spirit and your own conscience.

title: Proverbs 1:26
text: V. 26. Your fear-The misery you do or should fear.

title: Proverbs 1:28
text: V. 28. Early-With diligence and fervency.

title: Proverbs 1:29
text: V. 29. Knowledge-The practical knowledge of God and of their duty.

title: Proverbs 1:31
text: V. 31. Eat-They should receive punishment answerable to their sins. Filled-With the fruits of them.

title: Proverbs 1:32
text: V. 32. Turning-From God.  Destroy-Shall prove the occasion of their ruin, by making them presumptuous, and secure.

title: Proverbs 2:1
text:
CHAP. II. 
 
  Solomon shews, that they who diligently seek wisdom shall find it,   ver. 1-9.   He shews the advantage of it, that it would preserve them from evil   men, ver. 10-15.   And evil women, ver. 16-19.   And would lead them into, and keep them in the way of good men,   ver. 20-22. 
 
  V. 1. Hide-Lay them up in thy heart with care, as men do their choicest treasures.

title: Proverbs 2:3
text: V. 3. Criest-To God, the only giver of it.

title: Proverbs 2:4
text: V. 4. Seek her-With unwearied diligence and earnest desire and patient expectation.

title: Proverbs 2:8
text: V. 8. Path of judgment-Righteous paths, judgment being here put for righteousness.  And keeping of paths may be put for keeping them in their paths.

title: Proverbs 2:9
text: V. 9. Then-When God in answer to thy desires hath given thee wisdom. Equity-All the parts of thy duty to man, as well as the fear of God.

title: Proverbs 2:10
text: V. 10. When-Thou dost truly love wisdom.

title: Proverbs 2:13
text: V. 13. Darkness-Of sin.

title: Proverbs 2:15
text: V. 15. Crooked-Who swerve from the straight way of God's law, and have windings and turnings, to escape conviction.

title: Proverbs 2:16
text: V. 16. Strange woman-From the adulteress or whore.

title: Proverbs 2:17
text: V. 17. Forsaketh-Her husband whom she took to be her guide and governor, in her youth.  The covenant-The marriage covenant: so called because God is the author of that mutual obligation: and because God is called to be the witness and judge of that solemn promise and covenant.

title: Proverbs 2:18
text: V. 18. For-Conversation with her (which was most usual in her own house) is the certain way to death, which it brings many ways, and undoubtedly, without repentance, to God's wrath and the second death.

title: Proverbs 2:20
text: V. 20. That-This depends upon ver. Proverbs 2:11 , and is mentioned as another happy fruit of wisdom.

title: Proverbs 3:1
text:
CHAP. III. 
 
  An exhortation to be steadily religious, ver. 1-4.   To trust God, ver. 5, 6.   To fear him, ver. 7, 8.   To honour him with our substance, ver. 9, 10.   To bear affliction well, ver. 11-12.   The praise of wisdom, ver. 13-20.   The good effects of adhering to it, ver. 21-26.   Caution, against uncharitableness, strife, envy; if we would avoid a   curse and inherit a blessing, ver. 27-35. 
 
  V. 1. My law-The law of God, which might be called his law, as the gospel is called Paul's gospel,  II Timothy 2:8 , because delivered by him.

title: Proverbs 3:3
text: V. 3. Mercy-Mercy denotes all benignity, charity, and readiness to do good to others: truth or faithfulness respects all those duties which we owe to God or man, which we have special obligation from the rules of justice.  Bind them-Like a chain, wherewith persons adorn their necks. Table-In thy mind and heart, in which all God's commands are to be received and engraven.

title: Proverbs 3:4
text: V. 4. Understanding-Whereby to know thy duty, and to discern between good and evil.  Of God-Grace or favour with God, and that understanding which is good in God's sight.

title: Proverbs 3:5
text: V. 5. Trust-Wholly rely upon God's promises and providences. Lean not-Under this one kind of carnal confidence, he understands all other confidence in bodily strength, wealth, or friends.

title: Proverbs 3:8
text: V. 8. Navel-To thy body, which is signified by one part of it. Marrow-Which is the nourishment and strength of the bones.

title: Proverbs 3:9
text: V. 9. Substance-Lay out thy estate not to please thyself, but to glorify God.  First-fruits-Or, with the chief or best; which answers to the first-fruits under the law.

title: Proverbs 3:10
text: V. 10. So-This is not the way to diminish thy estate, but rather to increase it.

title: Proverbs 3:11
text: V. 11. Despise not-Either by making light of it, or not being duly affected with it; or by accounting it an unnecessary thing: but rather esteem it a privilege and favour from God.  Weary-Neither think it tedious or hard, but endure it with patience and chearfulness.

title: Proverbs 3:13
text: V. 13. Findeth-Which supposes his diligent searching for it.

title: Proverbs 3:17
text: V. 17. Peace-Procure a blessed tranquility in a man's mind and conscience.

title: Proverbs 3:18
text: V. 18. A tree-A pledge of everlasting life.  He alludes to the tree of life, and intimates, that this is the only restorer of that life which we have lost by sin.

title: Proverbs 3:19
text: V. 19. Wisdom-Either by Christ, or by that Divine perfection of wisdom, which is the fountain of wisdom in man.

title: Proverbs 3:20
text: V. 20. The depths-That great abyss contained in the bowels of the earth, breaks forth into fountains and rivers.

title: Proverbs 3:21
text: V. 21. Eyes-The eyes of thy mind.  Constantly and seriously meditate upon them.

title: Proverbs 3:22
text: V. 22. Grace-Like a beautiful chain or ornament.

title: Proverbs 3:25
text: V. 25. Be not-Thou shalt not be afraid.  Sudden-For sudden and unexpected evils are most frightful.  And fear is here put for the evils feared.  Desolation-Which cometh upon the wicked.

title: Proverbs 3:26
text: V. 26. Shall be-A sure ground of confidence to thee.  Taken-In the snares either of sin or mischief.

title: Proverbs 3:27
text: V. 27. With-hold not-Do not deny it, but readily and chearfuly impart it.  Good-Any thing which is good, either counsel, comfort, reproof, or the good things of the present life.  Due-That is, to all men, by that great and sovereign law of love.

title: Proverbs 3:28
text: V. 28. Say not-The former verse forbad the denial, and this forbids the delay of this duty.

title: Proverbs 3:29
text: V. 29. Securely-Relying upon thine integrity.

title: Proverbs 3:31
text: V. 31. Envy not-For his impunity and success.

title: Proverbs 3:32
text: V. 32. Abomination-Therefore sooner or later he must be miserable. The righteous-They are God's friends, to whom he imparts the favours and comforts to which other men are strangers.

title: Proverbs 3:33
text: V. 33. The house-Not only upon his own person, but also upon his posterity.

title: Proverbs 3:35
text: V. 35. Shame-Instead of that glory which they seek.

title: Proverbs 4:1
text:
CHAP. IV. 
 
  An exhortation to the study of wisdom, is forced by various arguments,   ver. 1-13.   A caution against bad company, ver. 14-19.   Directions for the attaining and keeping of wisdom, ver. 20-27. 
 
  V. 1. A father-Of me, who have paternal authority over you and affection for you.

title: Proverbs 4:3
text: V. 3. Tender-Young and tender in years, and tenderly educated. Only beloved-Beloved above all the rest.

title: Proverbs 4:4
text: V. 4. Said-The following verses, at least as far as the tenth verse, are the words of David.

title: Proverbs 4:7
text: V. 7. With all-Even with the price of all.

title: Proverbs 4:8
text: V. 8. Exalt-Let her have thine highest esteem and affection.

title: Proverbs 4:9
text: V. 9. Grace-A beautiful ornament, such as they used to put upon their heads.

title: Proverbs 4:16
text: V. 16. For-They cannot sleep with quietness.

title: Proverbs 4:17
text: V. 17. For-Wickedness is as pleasant to them as their bread.

title: Proverbs 4:18
text: V. 18. But-Just men daily grow in knowledge, and grace, and consolation, 'till all be perfected and swallowed up in glory.

title: Proverbs 4:19
text: V. 19. Darkness-Full of ignorance and error, of uncertainty and confusion, of danger and misery.

title: Proverbs 4:23
text: V. 23. Heart-Thy thoughts, will, and affections.  For-From thence proceed all the actions, as of the natural, so of the spiritual life, which lead to eternal life.

title: Proverbs 4:24
text: V. 24. Mouth-All sorts of sinful words.

title: Proverbs 4:25
text: V. 25. Right on-Direct all thine actions to a right end, and keep thy mind fixed upon that way which leads to it, and neither look or turn aside to the right-hand or the left.

title: Proverbs 4:26
text: V. 26. Ponder-Consider thine actions before thou dost them, and see that they agree with the rule.  And-Let thine actions be uniformly and constantly good in spite of all temptations.

title: Proverbs 5:1
text:
CHAP. V. 
 
  A farther exhortation to wisdom, ver. 1, 2.   A caution against whoredom, ver. 3-14.   Remedies against it, ver. 15-23.

title: Proverbs 5:3
text: V. 3. The lips-It concerns thee to get and to use discretion, that thou mayest be able to resist those temptations to which thou art exposed.

title: Proverbs 5:4
text: V. 4. But-The effect of that to which she entices men, is destruction.

title: Proverbs 5:5
text: V. 5. Feet-Her manner of life.

title: Proverbs 5:6
text: V. 6. Lest-To prevent thy serious consideration.  Moveable-She transforms herself into several shapes, and has a thousand arts to ensnare.  Know-Thou canst not discover all her practice.

title: Proverbs 5:9
text: V. 9. Honour-Thy dignity and reputation, the strength of thy body and mind.  Years-The flower of thine age.  The cruel-To the harlot, who though she pretends love, yet in truth is one of the most cruel creatures in the world, wasting thy estate and body without pity, and damming thy soul for ever.

title: Proverbs 5:10
text: V. 10. Strangers-Not only the strange women themselves, but others who are in league with them.  Labors-Wealth gotten by thy labours.

title: Proverbs 5:14
text: V. 14. A moment-In how little a time am I now come into remediless misery!  Assembly-And that in the congregation of Israel, where I was taught better things.

title: Proverbs 5:15
text: V. 15. Drink-Content thyself with those delights which God alloweth thee in the sober use of the marriage-bed.

title: Proverbs 5:16
text: V. 16. Fountains-Thy children proceeding from thy wife and from thyself.  Fountains are here put for rivers flowing from them. Dispersed-They shall in due time appear abroad to thy comfort, and for the good of others.

title: Proverbs 5:18
text: V. 18. Fountain-Thy wife.  Blessed-With children; for barrenness was esteemed a curse among the Israelites.

title: Proverbs 5:19
text: V. 19. Satisfy thee-At all convenient times: for that there may be excess in the marriage-bed is manifest.  Ravished-Love her fervently. It is an hyperbolical expression.

title: Proverbs 5:22
text: V. 22. Holden-He is in perfect bondage to his lusts, and is neither able nor wiling to set himself at liberty.

title: Proverbs 5:23
text: V. 23. Die-He shall die in his sins.  Astray-From the way of life, and from eternal salvation.

title: Proverbs 6:1
text:
CHAP. VI. 
 
  A caution against suretyship, ver. 1-5.   Against slothfulness, ver. 6-11.   The practice and end of a mischievous man, ver. 12-15.   Account of seven things which God hates, ver. 16-19.   An exhortation to keep the commandments, ver. 20-23.   Farther warnings against whoredom, ver. 24-35. 
 
  V. 1. Surety-Rashly, without considering how thou shalt discharge the debt as occasion require.  Otherwise suretyship in some cases may be not only lawful, but an act of justice and charity. Stricken thy hand-Obliged thyself by giving thine hand, as the custom then was in such cases.  With-With the creditor, whom he calls a stranger, because the usurers in Israel, who lent money to others, upon condition of paying use for it, were either Heathens, or were reputed as bad as Heathens, because this practice was forbidden by God's law,  Deuteronomy 23:19 .

title: Proverbs 6:3
text: V. 3. Hand-Into the power.  Friend-Of the debtor, for whom, as being thy friend, thou didst become surety; whereby thou art in his power, by his neglect or unfaithfulness, to expose thee to the payment of the debt.  Make sure-Or, and prevail with thy friend, strive to win him by thine incessant and earnest solicitations.

title: Proverbs 6:4
text: V. 4. Give not sleep-Until thou hast taken care for the discharge of this obligation.

title: Proverbs 6:6
text: V. 6. Go-This is a distinct precept; and it is for the most part as needless to seek, as hard to find, coherence in the proverbs.

title: Proverbs 6:11
