text: V. 11. Travelleth-Swiftly and unexpectedly. Armed man-Irresistibly.

title: Proverbs 6:16
text: V. 16. Hate-Above many other sins which have a worse name in the world.

title: Proverbs 6:18
text: V. 18. Deviseth-He whose practice it is to contrive wickedness. Swift-Such as greedily execute their wicked designs.

title: Proverbs 6:20
text: V. 20. The law-The word of God, which thy parents delivered to thee.

title: Proverbs 6:21
text: V. 21. Bind them-Constantly remember, and duly consider them.

title: Proverbs 6:22
text: V. 22. It-The law of God which thy parents have taught thee. Talk-It shall give thee counsel and comfort.

title: Proverbs 6:25
text: V. 25. Eye-lids-With her wanton glances,

title: Proverbs 6:30
text: V. 30. Despise-Abhor, but rather pity him.

title: Proverbs 6:31
text: V. 31. Restore-He speaks not of that restitution which the law required, but of that which either the wronged person might force the thief to make, or which the thief would willingly give rather than be exposed to public shame.

title: Proverbs 6:34
text: V. 34. Rage-It enflames a man with rage.  In the day-When he hath an opportunity to avenge himself.

title: Proverbs 7:1
text:
CHAP. VII. 
 
  An exhortation to cleave to wisdom, as a preservative from strange   women, ver. 1-5.   The snares they lay for unwary young men, ver. 6-23.   A serious caution against coming near them, ver. 24-27.

title: Proverbs 7:2
text: V. 2. Live-Thou shalt live.  Eye-With all possible care and diligence.

title: Proverbs 7:3
text: V. 3. Bind them-As a ring which is continually in a man's eye.

title: Proverbs 7:4
text: V. 4. And call-Acquaint and delight thyself with her.

title: Proverbs 7:8
text: V. 8. Passing-Idle and careless, near the corner of the street in which her house stood.

title: Proverbs 7:12
text: V. 12. Without-Without the door of her house.  Corner-Of the streets, where she might either conceal or discover herself, as she saw fit.

title: Proverbs 7:14
text: V. 14. Offerings-I have paid my peace-offerings which I had vowed. Whereby she signifies, that she had plentiful provisions at her house for his entertainment. For the peace-offerings were to be of the best flesh,  Leviticus 22:21 , and a considerable part of these offerings fell to the offerer's share.

title: Proverbs 7:20
text: V. 20. Hath taken-Which is an evidence that he designs to stay a considerable time.  At the day-So that we need not fear any surprise.

title: Proverbs 7:22
text: V. 22. As an ox-Going to it securely, as if it were going to a good pasture.

title: Proverbs 7:23
text: V. 23. His liver-His vital parts, 'till his life be lost.

title: Proverbs 8:1
text:
CHAP. VIII. 
 
  A recommendation of Divine wisdom, ver. 1-21.   The praise of the Son of God, the eternal Wisdom of the Father,   ver. 22-31.   An exhortation to hearken to him, ver. 32-36. 
 
  V. 1. Wisdom-It is a great question what this wisdom is.  Some understand it of the Divine wisdom; others of the second person in the Godhead: and it cannot be denied that some passages best agree to the former, and others to the latter opinion.  Possibly both may be joined together, and the chapter may be understood of Christ considered partly in his personal capacity, and partly in regard of his office, which was to impart the mind and will of God to mankind.

title: Proverbs 8:2
text: V. 2. High place-Where she may be best seen and heard.  Paths-Where many paths meet, where there is a great concourse, and where travellers may need direction.

title: Proverbs 8:3
text: V. 3. Gates-The places of judgment, and of the confluence of people. The entry-To invite passengers at their first coming and to conduct them to her house.  The doors-Of her house.

title: Proverbs 8:4
text: V. 4. O men-To all men without exception.

title: Proverbs 8:5
text: V. 5. Ye simple-Who want knowledge, and experience. Fools-Wilful sinners.

title: Proverbs 8:9
text: V. 9. To him-Whose mind God hath enlightened. To them-That are truly wise.

title: Proverbs 8:10
text: V. 10. And not silver-Rather than silver.

title: Proverbs 8:12
text: V. 12. I dwell-My inseparable companion is prudence to govern all my actions, and to direct the actions of others.  Find out-I help men to find out.  Inventions-Of all ingenious contrivances for the glory of God, and for the good of men.

title: Proverbs 8:14
text: V. 14. Wisdom-All solid and substantial and useful wisdom is assential to me.

title: Proverbs 8:15
text: V. 15. By me-They rule their kingdoms wisely and justly, by my counsel and assistance.  Their injustice is from themselves, but all the good they do, they owe to my conduct.

title: Proverbs 8:17
text: V. 17. I love-I do not despise their love, but kindly accept it and recompence it with my love and favour.  Early-With sincere affection and diligence, which he mentions as the evidence of their love.

title: Proverbs 8:21
text: V. 21. Substance-Substantial happiness: opposed to all worldly enjoyments, which are but mere shadows.

title: Proverbs 8:22
text: V. 22. Possessed me-As his son by eternal generation, before the beginning.  Of old-His works of creation.

title: Proverbs 8:23
text: V. 23. Set up-Heb. anointed, constituted to be the person by whom the Father resolved to do all his works, to create, to uphold and govern and judge, to redeem and save the world.  From the beginning-Before which, there was nothing but a vast eternity.  The earth-Which together with the heaven, was the first of God's visible works.

title: Proverbs 8:24
text: V. 24. No depths-No abyss or deep waters.  Brought forth-Begotten of my father.

title: Proverbs 8:26
text: V. 26. The earth-The dry land called earth after it was separated from the waters  Genesis 1:10 . Fields-The plain and open parts of the earth distinguished from the mountains.  Dust-Of this lower part of the world which consists of dust.

title: Proverbs 8:27
text: V. 27. I was there-As co-worker with my Father.  Depth-Of that great abyss of water and earth mixed together, which is called both earth and water and the deep,  Genesis 1:2 , when he made this lower world in the form of a globe.

title: Proverbs 8:28
text: V. 28. Strengthened-When he shut up the fountains in the cavities of the earth, and kept them there as it were by a strong band. The deep-Which have their original from the deep, either from the sea, or from the abyss of waters in the bowels of the earth.

title: Proverbs 8:31
text: V. 31. My delights were-To uphold them by my power and providence, to reveal myself and my Father's will to them from age to age, to assume their nature, and to redeem and save them.

title: Proverbs 8:34
text: V. 34. Waiting-As servants or clients, wait at the doors of princes or persons of eminency.

title: Proverbs 9:1
text:
CHAP. IX. 
 
  Christ, under the name of wisdom invites us to his entertainment,   ver. 1-6.   Foretells the different successes of his invitation, ver. 7-9.   Shews the fruit of fearing God, ver. 10-12.   Sin, in the person of a foolish woman invites us to her entertainment,   ver. 13-17.   Which ends in destruction, ver. 18 
 
  V. 1. Her house-For the reception of her guests.  Seven-Many pillars; whereby is intimated the beauty and stability of the church. Pillars-Prophets, and apostles, and ministers.

title: Proverbs 9:2
text: V. 2. Killed-Made provision for the guests.  Mingled-With water, as they used to do in those hot countries.  Furnished-With all necessaries, and now waits for the guests.

title: Proverbs 9:3
text: V. 3. Maidens-Her servants to invite the guests, ministers of the word whom he calls maidens for the decency of the parable; for wisdom being compared to a great princess, was fit to be attended upon by maidens. Highest places-From such high seats as those from which judges delivered their sentences, and officers made proclamations.

title: Proverbs 9:4
text: V. 4. Simple-Ignorant, and weak.

title: Proverbs 9:7
text: V. 7. A former-He shews whom he meant by the foolish, ver. Proverbs 9:6 , even scorners and wicked men, and presses his last advice of forsaking them because there was no good, but hurt to be got from them.

title: Proverbs 9:8
text: V. 8. A scorner-An obstinate and incorrigible sinner.

title: Proverbs 9:12
text: V. 12. For thyself-Thou dost not profit me but thyself.

title: Proverbs 9:14
text: V. 14. At the door-Watching for occasions of sin.

title: Proverbs 9:15
text: V. 15. Go right-Who are going innocently about their business.

title: Proverbs 9:16
text: V. 16. Simple-This title is not given them by her, but by Solomon.

title: Proverbs 9:17
text: V. 17. Sweet-From the difficulty of obtaining them; and because the very prohibition renders them more grateful to corrupt nature.

title: Proverbs 10:1
text:
CHAP. X. 
 
  Here the Proverbs, properly so called, begin.   They are short, but   weighty sentences, most of which are two sentences in one verse,   illustrating each other.   But it is seldom there is any coherence   between the verses, much less any thread of discourse.

title: Proverbs 10:2
text: V. 2. Of wickedness-Such as are got by any sort of wicked practices. Death-Often from temporal, and always from eternal death.

title: Proverbs 10:5
text: V. 5. Gathereth-The fruits of his field.  In summer-In harvest. He that improved the opportunities of doing good to himself and others.

title: Proverbs 10:6
text: V. 6. Violence-Their own violence or injustice.  This may be an allusion to the ancient custom of covering the mouths and faces of condemned malefactors.

title: Proverbs 10:8
text: V. 8. Who receive-Is ready to hear and obey the precepts of God and men.  Fall-Into mischief.

title: Proverbs 10:9
text: V. 9. Surely-Or, securely, or confidently, as the word properly signifies; quietly resting upon God's favour and gracious providence for his protections.  Known-His wickedness shall be publickly discovered.

title: Proverbs 10:10
text: V. 10. Winketh-That secretly designs mischief against others, as this phrase is used,  Psalms 35:19 .

title: Proverbs 10:13
text: V. 13. Wisdom-This wisdom shews itself in his speech. A rod-Rebukes from God and men.

title: Proverbs 10:14
text: V. 14. Lay up-In their minds, to be brought forth upon fit occasions. Knowledge-Whereby they may be enabled to speak both what, and when it is seasonable.  But-Fools are more forward to lay out than to lay up, and for want of knowledge speak much and foolishly, whereby they frequently bring destruction upon themselves.

title: Proverbs 10:15
text: V. 15. Wealth-It often redeems him from dangers and calamities. Poverty-Is the cause of their ruin.

title: Proverbs 10:16
text: V. 16. The labour-The fruit of his labour, to the preservation of this life, and obtaining eternal life.  Fruit-The fruit of all their labour tends to sin, and serves only for fuel to mens pride and luxury.

title: Proverbs 10:18
text: V. 18. Lying lips-With flattering words. He here condemns two opposite vices, secret hatred, and manifest slander.

title: Proverbs 10:20
text: V. 20. Is-Of great worth and use.  Heart-And consequently the tongue.

title: Proverbs 10:21
text: V. 21. Feed-By their wise discourses and counsels.  Die-They have not wisdom to preserve themselves, much less to feed others.

title: Proverbs 10:26
text: V. 26. So-Unserviceable and vexatious.

title: Proverbs 10:28
text: V. 28. Gladness-Shall be accomplished, and turned into enjoyment.

title: Proverbs 10:29
text: V. 29. The way-The way of God's precepts.  Strength-Gives strength, support, and protection.

title: Proverbs 10:30
text: V. 30. Never be removed-They shall live happily here, and eternally in heaven.  The earth-They shall not have so much as a quiet abode upon earth; much less shall they have any possession in heaven.

title: Proverbs 10:32
text: V. 32. The lips-Knowledge is here ascribed to the lips, as it is to the hands,  Psalms 78:72 , because they are conducted by knowledge and wisdom.  Acceptable-What is truly worthy of acceptation.

title: Proverbs 11:1
text:
CHAP. XI. 
 
  V. 1. A false balance-The use of all false weights and measures in commerce.

title: Proverbs 11:8
text: V. 8. Cometh-Into trouble.

title: Proverbs 11:9
text: V. 9. Delivered-From the infection of the hypocrite's evil counsel.

title: Proverbs 11:11
text: V. 11. The blessing-Wherewith they bless the city, by their sincere prayers, and wise and wholesome counsels.  The mouth-By their curses, and oaths, and blasphemies, and wicked counsels.

title: Proverbs 11:12
text: V. 12. Despiseth-Which he shews by contemptuous or reproachful expressions.  Holdeth peace-Forbears all such expressions, and silently and patiently bears those reproaches.

title: Proverbs 11:13
text: V. 13. Secrets-Such things as were committed to his trust with a charge of secrecy.

title: Proverbs 11:16
text: V. 16. Gracious woman-A woman endued with the grace of God. Retaineth-Or, holdeth fast her honour, or reputation.

title: Proverbs 11:18
text: V. 18. Worketh-A work which will deceive his expectation. Soweth-That worketh it with constancy, and diligence.

title: Proverbs 11:21
text: V. 21. Though hand join-Though they are fortified against God's judgments by a numerous issue and kindred, and friends, and by mutual and strong combinations.  The seed-Not only their persons, but their children.

title: Proverbs 11:22
text: V. 22. So is a fair woman without discretion-     "Of beauty vain, of virtue void,      What art thou in the sight of God?      A slave to every base desire,      A creature wallowing in the mire.      Go, gaudy pageant of a day,      Thy folly, with thy face display:      Set all thy charms and graces out,      And shew - the Jewel in thy snout!"

title: Proverbs 11:23
text: V. 23. The desire-The desires and expectations of the righteous shall end in their happiness, but the desires and expectations of the wicked men shall be disappointed, and end in the wrath of God.

title: Proverbs 11:24
text: V. 24. Scattereth-That gives liberally.  Increaseth-Through God's blessing upon his estate.  Poverty-By God's providence secretly blasting his estate.

title: Proverbs 11:25
text: V. 25. Fat-Shall be enriched both with temporal and spiritual blessings.

title: Proverbs 11:26
text: V. 26. With-holdeth corn-In a time of scarcity.  Selleth-Upon reasonable terms.

title: Proverbs 11:27
text: V. 27. Seeketh-To do good to all men.  Favour-With God and men.

title: Proverbs 11:29
text: V. 29. Troubleth-He who brings trouble upon himself and children, either by prodigality, or by restless endeavours to heap up riches. Wind-Shall be as unable to keep what he gets as a man is to hold the wind in his hand.

title: Proverbs 11:30
text: V. 30. The fruit-His discourses and his whole conversation, is like the fruit of the tree of life.  Winneth-That gains souls to God.

title: Proverbs 11:31
text: V. 31. Recompensed-Punished for his sins.

title: Proverbs 12:6
text:
CHAP. XII. 
 
  V. 6. Lie in wait-Are designed to entrap others, and to destroy them. Deliver them-From those that lie in wait for them.

title: Proverbs 12:7
text: V. 7. Are not-Both they and their families suddenly perish.

title: Proverbs 12:9
text: V. 9. Despised-That lives in a mean condition.  Honoureth-That glories in his high birth or gay attire.

title: Proverbs 12:10
text: V. 10. Regardeth-He will not destroy it either by labour beyond its strength, or by denying it necessary food or rest.  Cruel-There is cruelty mixed even with their most merciful actions.

title: Proverbs 12:11
text: V. 11. Tilleth-That employs his time in an honest calling. Vain persons-In an idle course of living.

title: Proverbs 12:12
text: V. 12. Desireth-He approves those arts, which wicked men use like nets to ensnare other men.  The root-That piety, which is the root of his actions, yields him sufficient fruit both for his own need, and to do good to others.

title: Proverbs 12:14
text: V. 14. Mouth-By his pious and profitable discourses.  Hands-Of his actions.

title: Proverbs 12:15
text: V. 15. Hearkeneth-That distrusts his own judgments, and seeks counsel from others.

title: Proverbs 12:16
text: V. 16. Covereth-The shame, or injury done to him, which he conceals and bears with patience.

title: Proverbs 12:17
text: V. 17. Deceit-He who uses himself to lying in his common talk, will use falsehood and deceit in judgment.

title: Proverbs 12:18
text: V. 18. Health-Tends to the comfort and benefit of others.

title: Proverbs 12:19
text: V. 19. A moment-Liars, though they may make a fair shew for a season, yet are quickly convicted.

title: Proverbs 12:20
text: V. 20. Deceit-They whose hearts devise mischief shall be deceived in their hopes, and bring trouble upon themselves: but they who by good counsels labour to promote peace, shall reap the comfort of it themselves.

title: Proverbs 12:23
text: V. 23. Concealeth-He does not unseasonably utter what he knows. Foolishness-Betrays his ignorance and folly.

title: Proverbs 12:25
text: V. 25. A good word-A compassionate or encouraging word.

title: Proverbs 12:26
text: V. 26. Neighbour-Than any other men.  Seduceth-Heb. maketh them to err, to lose that excellency or happiness which they had promised themselves.

title: Proverbs 12:27
text: V. 27. Resteth not-Does not enjoy the fruit of his labours. Precious-Yields him comfort and blessing with it.

title: Proverbs 13:2
text:
CHAP. XIII. 
 
  V. 2. Shall eat-Shall receive comfort, and benefit by his wise and profitable discourses.

title: Proverbs 13:6
text: V. 6. Keepeth him-From that over-throw which befal sinners.

title: Proverbs 13:7
text: V. 7. Maketh rich-Some men who have little or nothing, pretend to have great riches.  Maketh rich-Some rich men profess to be poor.

title: Proverbs 13:8
text: V. 8. Riches-Riches enable a man to redeem his life when it is in greatest danger, and poverty preserves a man from many injuries.  Because they are cautious, that they may not provoke others; and because they are esteemed objects of pity.

title: Proverbs 13:9
text: V. 9. The light-The prosperity.  Rejoiceth-Shines with a pleasant and constant brightness.  Rejoicing is here ascribed to the light, as it is to the sun,  Psalms 19:5 , metaphorically. Put out-Their felicity shall have a hidden end.

title: Proverbs 13:10
text: V. 10. Pride-It is chiefly, pride which blows up the coals of contention.  Well-advised-Who are not governed by their passions, but by prudent considerations.  Wisdom-Which teaches them to avoid contention.

title: Proverbs 13:11
text: V. 11. Vanity-By wicked practices.

title: Proverbs 13:12
text: V. 12. Hope deferred-Delays in obtaining what a man passionately desires.  The desire-The good desired.  A tree of life-It is satisfactory, and reviving.

title: Proverbs 13:13
text: V. 13. The word-The word of God.

title: Proverbs 13:14
text: V. 14. The law-The instruction, or counsel; as the word law, is frequently understood in scripture.

title: Proverbs 13:15
text: V. 15. Giveth-Makes a man acceptable to God.  Rough-Offensive and hateful to God and men, as rough ways are to a traveller.

title: Proverbs 13:16
text: V. 16. Knowledge-Considerately and discreetly.  Layeth open-By his foolish actions.

title: Proverbs 13:17
text: V. 17. A messenger-Who is unfaithful in the execution of that which is committed to his charge.  Is health-Procures benefit, as to his master, so to himself.

title: Proverbs 13:19
text: V. 19. Sweet-Whatsoever men earnestly desire, the enjoyment of it is sweet to them; therefore sinners rejoice in the satisfaction of their sinful lusts, and abhor all restraint of them.

title: Proverbs 13:21
text: V. 21. Evil-Punishment proportionable to their sin.

title: Proverbs 13:23
text: V. 23. The poor-Poor persons by their diligent labours, and God's blessing often grow rich.  Destroyed-Or, consumed, brought to poverty, for want of discretion.

title: Proverbs 13:24
text: V. 24. Hateth his son-His fond affection, is as pernicious to him as hatred.

title: Proverbs 14:1
text:
CHAP. XIV. 
 
  V. 1. Buildeth-Maintains and improves her family and estate. Her hands-By her idleness or sin.

title: Proverbs 14:3
text: V. 3. A rod-His insolent speeches as they are like a rod, offensive to others, so, they make a rod for their own backs.

title: Proverbs 14:4
text: V. 4. The crib-The stable is empty of food for cattle, and much more for man.  In the same sense cleanness of teeth is put for famine,  Amos 4:6 . The strength-By their labours, or by diligence in husbandry, which then was principally managed by oxen.

title: Proverbs 14:6
text: V. 6. Findeth it not-Because he doth not seek it aright.  That understandeth-That is honest and pious.

title: Proverbs 14:8
text: V. 8. His way-Consists not in vain speculations, but in a diligent study of his duty, and of the way to eternal happiness.  The folly-The wit of ungodly men, which is really their folly, is employed only in finding out ways of deceiving.

title: Proverbs 14:9
text: V. 9. Favour-They find favour both with God and men.

title: Proverbs 14:10
text: V. 10. Bitterness-The inward griefs and joys of mens hearts, are not known to any but a man's self.

title: Proverbs 14:12
text: V. 12. Right-There are some evil courses which men may think to be lawful and good.  The end-The event shews that they were sinful and destructive.

title: Proverbs 14:13
text: V. 13. In laughter-The outward signs of joy are often mixed with real sorrow.

title: Proverbs 14:14
text: V. 14. In heart-He who departs from God inwardly.  Filled-With the fruit of his ways, the punishment of his sins.  Satisfied-From the pious temper of his own heart, which cleaves to the Lord, he shall receive unspeakable comfort.

title: Proverbs 14:15
text: V. 15. The simple-A foolish man.  Looketh-He orders his dealings in the world with due circumspection, not considering so much what other men say as what he ought to do.

title: Proverbs 14:16
text: V. 16. Feareth-Trembles at God's judgments when they are either inflicted or threatened.  Rageth-Frets against God; or is enraged against his messengers.  Confident-Secure and insensible of his danger.

title: Proverbs 14:17
text: V. 17. Foolishly-His passion hurries him into foolish speeches and actions.  Wicked devices-One who suppresses his passion, but meditates revenge.  Hated-Both by God and men.

title: Proverbs 14:18
text: V. 18. Inherit-They possess it as their inheritance, holding it fast, and glorying in it.  Knowledge-The saving knowledge of God and of their own duty.

title: Proverbs 14:19
text: V. 19. The evil-Good men shall have the pre-eminency over the wicked.

title: Proverbs 14:20
text: V. 20. Hated-Despised and abandoned.

title: Proverbs 14:21
text: V. 21. Despiseth-That does not pity and relieve the poor.

title: Proverbs 14:23
text: V. 23. The talk-Idle talking will bring a man to poverty.

title: Proverbs 14:24
text: V. 24. Riches-They are a singular advantage and ornament to them. But-As for rich fools, their folly is not cured, but made worse and more manifest by their riches.

title: Proverbs 14:25
text: V. 25. Souls-Such as are innocent, from false accusations.

title: Proverbs 14:27
text: V. 27. To depart-To preserve men from destructive courses.

title: Proverbs 14:29
text: V. 29. Exalteth-Heb. lifteth up, like a banner, makes it known and visible to all men.

title: Proverbs 14:30
text: V. 30. A sound heart-Free from envy and inordinate passions. Is life-Procures and maintains the health and vigour of the body.

title: Proverbs 14:31
text: V. 31. His maker-Whose image the poor man bears, by whose providence he is made poor, and who hath declared himself to be their protector and avenger.

title: Proverbs 14:32
text: V. 32. Driven away-In his death, from God's favour and presence. Death-In his greatest dangers and distresses, yea even in death itself.

title: Proverbs 14:33
text: V. 33. Resteth-Is laid up and hid there.  In the midst-In the heart.  Made known-They will publish in all times and companies.

title: Proverbs 14:35
text: V. 35. Shame-Both to himself, by his foolish management of the king's affairs, and to the king who made so foolish a choice of a servant.

title: Proverbs 15:2
text:
CHAP. XV. 
 
  V. 2. Aright-Expressing what he knows prudently and gracefully. Poureth out-Plentifully, continually, and vehemently, as a fountain does waters.

title: Proverbs 15:4
text: V. 4. Wholesome-Which utters sound and useful counsels.  Tree of life-Is greatly useful to preserve the present life, and to promote the spiritual and eternal life, both of the speaker and hearers. Perverseness-False or corrupt speeches.  A breach-Disturbs and wounds the spirits, both of the speaker and hearers.

title: Proverbs 15:6
text: V. 6. Revenues-Though he may obtain great revenues, yet they are attended with much trouble.

title: Proverbs 15:7
text: V. 7. Disperse-Freely communicate to others what they know.

title: Proverbs 15:8
text: V. 8. Sacrifice-All the religious services, yea, the most costly; one kind being put for all the rest.  Prayer-The cheapest and meanest services.

title: Proverbs 15:11
text: V. 11. Destruction-The place of destruction, of which men know nothing but by Divine revelation.

title: Proverbs 15:14
text: V. 14. Foolishness-Wickedness is meat and drink to them.

title: Proverbs 15:15
text: V. 15. Afflicted-Of the troubled in mind.  Evil-Tedious and uncomfortable.  Chearful-Heb. of a good heart.

title: Proverbs 15:16
text: V. 16. Trouble-Tumultuous lusts and passions, vexatious cares, and horrors of conscience.

title: Proverbs 15:19
text: V. 19. An hedge-As a way hedged up with thorns, troublesome, perplexed, and full of difficulties.  Plain-Is easy and pleasant to him, notwithstanding all its difficulties.

title: Proverbs 15:22
text: V. 22. Counsel-When men do not seek, or will not receive advice from others.

title: Proverbs 15:23
text: V. 23. The answer-By a wise, or good and seasonable answer.

title: Proverbs 15:24
text: V. 24. The way-The way a wise man takes to obtain life, is to place his heart, and treasure, and conversation on things above.

title: Proverbs 15:25
text: V. 25. The proud-Of the mighty oppressors.  The border-The estate, the border being often used, for the land within the borders.

title: Proverbs 15:26
text: V. 26. Pleasant-Acceptable to God.

title: Proverbs 15:27
text: V. 27. Troubleth-Brings God's curse upon himself and family. Gifts-Bribes given to corrupt judgment.  Live-Shall preserve himself and family from ruin.

title: Proverbs 15:28
text: V. 28. Studieth-He speaks considerately.  The mouth-Not the heart; for he rashly speaks what comes into his mouth, without the direction of his heart or conscience.

title: Proverbs 15:30
text: V. 30. A good report-A good name.  Fat-Not only chears a man for the present, but gives him such stable comfort as revives his soul, and gives vigour to his body.

title: Proverbs 15:31
text: V. 31. The ear-The man that hearkens to that reproof which leads to life, seeks and delights in the company of the wise.

title: Proverbs 15:33
text: V. 33. The instruction-Doth instruct men in true wisdom.

title: Proverbs 16:1
text:
CHAP. XVI. 
 
  V. 1. From the Lord-Men can neither think nor speak wisely and well without Divine assistance.

title: Proverbs 16:2
text: V. 2. Weigheth-Exactly knows as men do the things which they weigh. Spirits-The hearts of men.

title: Proverbs 16:3
text: V. 3. Commit-Refer all thy actions and concerns to God, as the end of them, and depend upon God's providence for success.  Established-Thy designs shall be brought to an happy issue.

title: Proverbs 16:4
text: V. 4. Doth work-He orders or disposes.  For-For his own glory; for the discovery of his wisdom, power, goodness, truth, justice. The wicked-Wilful and impenitent sinners.  Men make themselves wicked, and God therefore makes them miserable.

title: Proverbs 16:6
text: V. 6. By mercy-By a merciful and just and faithful frame of heart and course of life.  Is purged-As they qualify a man to offer up acceptable prayers to God for the pardon of his sins.  By fear-By a filial reverence unto God.  Depart-They are kept from abusing pardoning mercy, and from returning to folly or wickedness.

title: Proverbs 16:9
text: V. 9. Deviseth-Proposes what he will do.  Directeth-Over-rules and disposes all his designs and actions.

title: Proverbs 16:10
text: V. 10. A divine sentence-Great sagacity and piercing judgment. Of the king-Of wise kings; who only are worthy of that name and office.

title: Proverbs 16:11
text: V. 11. The Lord's-Are made by his direction and appointment, so that no man can alter them without violating God's rights and authority.

title: Proverbs 16:15
text: V. 15. A cloud-As acceptable as those clouds which bring the latter rain, whereby the fruits are filled and ripened a little before the harvest.

title: Proverbs 16:17
text: V. 17. The high-way-Their common road, in which they walk, tho' through frailty or temptation they slip into the bypath of sin. From evil-From the evil of sin, and consequently from the evil of punishment.  Keepeth-That takes heed to walk in that high-way.

title: Proverbs 16:20
text: V. 20. Good-He who orders his affairs with discretion.

title: Proverbs 16:21
text: V. 21. The wise-He who is truly wise, shall be so accounted by others. Sweetness-Eloquence added to wisdom.  Increaseth-Both in himself, for while a man teaches others, he improves himself; and others, who by this means are induced to hear and receive his instructions.

title: Proverbs 16:22
text: V. 22. The instruction-Their most grave and serious counsels are foolish.

title: Proverbs 16:23
text: V. 23. Teacheth-Directs him what to speak, and keeps him from speaking foolishly.  Addeth-Enables him to speak learnedly and wisely.

title: Proverbs 16:27
text: V. 27. Diggeth up-Prosecutes his evil designs with great industry. His lips-His tongue is set on fire of hell.

title: Proverbs 16:30
text: V. 30. Shutteth-That his thoughts may be more intent. Moving-Which is the gesture of one whose thoughts are deeply engaged.

title: Proverbs 16:32
text: V. 32. Is better-Of a more gallant and generous spirit, and more valiant and victorious.

title: Proverbs 16:33
text: V. 33. The lot-As the ancient practice was in deciding doubtful things. The event of which though casual to men, is directed by God's providence.

title: Proverbs 17:4
text:
CHAP. XVII. 
 
  V. 4. False lips-To false accusations and calumnies, which give him occasion and encouragement to do mischief.

title: Proverbs 17:7
text: V. 7. Excellent speech-Discourse of high and excellent things.

title: Proverbs 17:8
text: V. 8. A precious stone-Pleasant and acceptable; and withal dazzles his eyes.  Whithersoever-To whomsoever it is presented.  But this, as also many of her proverbs, are to be understood of most men, not of all.

title: Proverbs 17:9
text: V. 9. Covereth-That conceals as far as he may, other mens faults.

title: Proverbs 17:11
text: V. 11. Rebellion-Against God.  Messenger-Or, a cruel angel, the angel of death, the devil, or some bloody men employed by God to avenge his quarrel.

title: Proverbs 17:12
text: V. 12. Folly-In the heat of his lust or passion.

title: Proverbs 17:14
text: V. 14. Letteth out-By cutting the bank of a river.  Leave off-Avoid the occasions, and prevent the beginning of contention.

title: Proverbs 17:16
text: V. 16. A price-Opportunities and abilities of getting it. No heart-Neither discretion to discern the worth of wisdom, nor any sincere desire to get it.

title: Proverbs 17:17
text: V. 17. Was born-Was sent into the world for this, that he might comfort and relieve his brother in adversity.

title: Proverbs 17:18
text: V. 18. Friend-Debtor, for whom being his friend, he becomes surety.

title: Proverbs 17:20
text: V. 20. No good-Shall not get that advantage which he expects.

title: Proverbs 17:22
text: V. 22. Doth good-Even to the body; it contributes much to bodily health and vigour.  Drieth-Wastes the marrow of the bones, and the moisture and strength of the body.

title: Proverbs 17:24
text: V. 24. In the face-His wisdom appears even in his looks. The eyes-Minding most, those things which are remotest from him, and least concern him.

title: Proverbs 17:26
text: V. 26. To strike-Nor to smite magistrates, either with the hand or tongue, for the execution of justice.

title: Proverbs 18:1
text:
CHAP. XVIII. 
 
  V. 1. Desire-Thro' desire of wisdom, a man having separated himself from the company, and noise, and business of the world, seeketh and intermeddleth with all wisdom, uses all diligence, that he may search and find out all solid knowledge and true wisdom.

title: Proverbs 18:2
text: V. 2. Understanding-In getting sound and saving, knowledge.  The discovery-In uttering that folly and wickedness which is in his heart.

title: Proverbs 18:3
text: V. 3. Cometh-Into any place or company.  Contempt-He despiseth all instruction and reproof.  Reproach-And he shews his contempt by ignominious and reproachful expressions.

title: Proverbs 18:4
text: V. 4. A man's-A wise man's.  As a brook-That wisdom which is in his heart is continually pouring forth wise and good counsels.

title: Proverbs 18:8
text: V. 8. They go-They wound mortally.

title: Proverbs 18:9
text: V. 9. Is brother-Though they take several paths, yet both come to one end.

title: Proverbs 18:10
text: V. 10. The name-The Lord, as he hath revealed himself in his works, and in his word by his promises.

title: Proverbs 18:14
text: V. 14. Sustain-Will easily support him under any outward troubles. Wounded-Dejected with the sense of its own guilt and misery.

title: Proverbs 18:18
text: V. 18. Parteth-Gives to every one what is right or meet.

title: Proverbs 18:20
text: V. 20. Satisfied-Wise discourses tend to the satisfaction of the speaker, as well as to the good of the hearers.

title: Proverbs 18:21
text: V. 21. Death and life-Are brought upon men by, the good or bad use of their tongues.  Lovest-That love much talking.

title: Proverbs 18:22
text: V. 22. A wise-A good wife; one that deserves the name, and performs the duty of that relation.  Favour-Obtains her not by his own diligence, but by God's good providence.

title: Proverbs 18:24
text: V. 24. A man-Heb. A man of friends; who desires the friendship of others.

title: Proverbs 19:2
text:
CHAP. XIX. 
 
  V. 2. Hasteth-That rashly and headily rushes into actions.

title: Proverbs 19:3
text: V. 3. Perverteth-Blasts his designs and enterprises.  Fretteth-He ascribes his unhappiness not to his own sin, but to God and his providence.

title: Proverbs 19:6
text: V. 6. A friend-in profession.

title: Proverbs 19:7
text: V. 7. Brethren-His nearest relations.  Hate-Despise and shun him. Pursueth-Earnestly imploring their pity.

title: Proverbs 19:10
text: V. 10. Delight-To live in pleasure and outward glory, doth not become him, nor suit with him; because prosperity corrupts even wise men, and makes fools mad; and because it gives him more opportunity to discover his folly, and to do mischief both to himself and others.

title: Proverbs 19:13
text: V. 13. Dropping-Are like rain continually dropping upon an house.

title: Proverbs 19:15
text: V. 15. Casteth-Makes a man careless, and like one asleep in his business.

title: Proverbs 19:16
text: V. 16. His ways-The commands of God.

title: Proverbs 19:18
text: V. 18. While-Before custom in sin, and thy indulgence have made him incorrigible.  Let not-Forbear not to give him due and necessary correction.

title: Proverbs 19:19
text: V. 19. Great wrath-Of strong passions.  Deliver-If thou forbear to punish him.  Do it-Thou must deliver him again and again.

title: Proverbs 19:22
text: V. 22. The desire-The hearty desire of being kind is accepted by God, and should be owned by men as a real kindness.  A poor man-Who is not able to give what he desires to do.  A liar-Than a rich man who feeds the poor with fair promises, but doth not perform what he pretends.

title: Proverbs 19:23
text: V. 23. Satisfied-Shall be fully contented with God's favour and blessing.

title: Proverbs 19:24
text: V. 24. Bring it-To feed himself; he expects that the meat should drop into his mouth.

title: Proverbs 19:25
text: V. 25. Scorner-An obstinate and impudent transgressor.  Simple-Who sin thro' ignorance, being possibly drawn to it by the scorner's evil counsel or example.  Reprove-A verbal reproof will be more effectual for his reformation, than the severest punishments will be to a scorner.

title: Proverbs 19:26
text: V. 26. Wasteth-His father's estate.  Chaseth-Causes her to avoid his presence, and to go from the house where he is.

title: Proverbs 19:28
text: V. 28. Scorneth-Hath no reverence to the place of justice, nor to the presence of God there.  Devoureth-Utters it with greediness and delight.

title: Proverbs 19:29
text: V. 29. Prepared-Although they be deferred for a time, yet they are treasured up for them.

title: Proverbs 20:1
text:
CHAP. XX. 
 
  V. 1. A mocker-Wine immoderately drunk makes men mockers. Raging-Makes men full of rage.

title: Proverbs 20:2
text: V. 2. The fear-The terror which the wrath of a king causes.

title: Proverbs 20:3
text: V. 3. Meddling-Is always ready to begin strife, and obstinate in the continuance of it.

title: Proverbs 20:5
text: V. 5. Counsel-Designs of doing something of moment. Deep water-Is secret and hard to be discovered.

title: Proverbs 20:8
text: V. 8. His eyes-With his very looks, or by his diligent inspection into affairs.

title: Proverbs 20:10
text: V. 10. Divers-One greater for shew and one lesser for use.

title: Proverbs 20:11
text: V. 11. Is known-The future disposition of a man may be probably conjectured from his childish manners.

title: Proverbs 20:13
text: V. 13. Open-Shake off sloth and betake thyself to thy employment with diligence and vigour.

title: Proverbs 20:15
text: V. 15. The lips-But wise speeches are of far greater worth.

title: Proverbs 20:16
text: V. 16. Take-As a pledge, without which he ought not to be trusted. Of him-That is surety.

title: Proverbs 20:18
text: V. 18. Established-The way to bring our purposes to good effect is to manage them with serious consideration.

title: Proverbs 20:20
text: V. 20. Lamp-His name and memory shall utterly perish.

title: Proverbs 20:24
text: V. 24. His way-What the issue of his designs will be.

title: Proverbs 20:25
text: V. 25. A snare-It brings guilt upon him.  After-After a man has made vows to enquire for ways to break them.

title: Proverbs 20:26
text: V. 26. The wheel-As the cart-wheel was anciently turned over the sheaves to beat the corn out of them.  He punishes them as their offences deserve.

title: Proverbs 20:27
text: V. 27. The spirit-The reasonable soul.  The candle-Is a clear and glorious light set up in man for his information and direction. Of the Lord-So called because it comes from God in a more immediate manner than the body,  Ecclesiastes 12:7 , and because it is in God's stead, to observe and judge all our actions.  Searching-Discerning not only his outward actions, which are visible to others, but his most inward thoughts and affections.  The belly is here put for the heart, as it is frequently.

title: Proverbs 20:30
text: V. 30. The blueness-Grievous wounds, which make men black and blue; or severe punishments.  Cleanseth-Are the means to reclaim a wicked man, and to purge out his corruption.  The belly-Of the heart.  Grievous wounds or stripes cleanse not only the outward man by keeping it from evil actions, but even the inward man, by expelling or subduing vile affections: which is a great and blessed benefit of afflictions.

title: Proverbs 21:1
text:
CHAP. XXI. 
 
  V. 1. The kings-He names kings not to exclude other men, but because they are more arbitrary and uncontrollable than others. As rivers-Which husband-men draw by little channels into the adjacent grounds as they please.

title: Proverbs 21:4
text: V. 4. The plowing-Even their civil or natural actions, which in themselves are lawful, are made sinful as they are managed by ungodly men, without any regard to the glory of God, which ought to be the end of all our actions.

title: Proverbs 21:5
text: V. 5. Hasty-Who manages his affairs rashly.

title: Proverbs 21:6
text: V. 6. Lying tongue-By any false or deceitful words or actions. Is tossed-Is like the chaff or smoak driven away by the wind. Of them-That take those courses which will bring destruction upon them.

title: Proverbs 21:8
text: V. 8. The way-Of every man by nature.  Strange-Estranged from God. Right-But he whose heart is pure, his conversation is agreeable to it.

title: Proverbs 21:10
text: V. 10. Desireth-To do mischief.  No favour-He spares neither friend nor foe.

title: Proverbs 21:11
text: V. 11. The wise-The simple learn wisdom, both from the punishment of wicked men, and from the prosperity of good men.

title: Proverbs 21:12
text: V. 12. Considereth-He looks through its present glory to that ruin for which it is designed.

title: Proverbs 21:14
text: V. 14. In secret-Which makes it more acceptable. In the bosom-Secretly conveyed into the bosom.

title: Proverbs 21:16
text: V. 16. Shall remain-Shall, without repentance, be condemned to eternal death.

title: Proverbs 21:17
text: V. 17. Wine and oil-Delicious fare and luxurious feasting.  Wine and oil were much used in feasts in those parts.

title: Proverbs 21:18
text: V. 18. A ransom-The wicked shall be brought into those troubles, which were designed by wicked men for the righteous: thus Haman was a ransom for Mordecai.

title: Proverbs 21:20
text: V. 20. The wise-Wise men lay up desirable treasures for their own use, and for their families.  Oil is particularly mentioned, because that was a considerable part of their wealth and treasures in those countries.

title: Proverbs 21:22
text: V. 22. The strength-The strongest sorts to which the citizens trust.

title: Proverbs 21:25
text: V. 25. Killeth-Torments him to death, while he passionately desires what he sees, he shall not enjoy, and will not take pains to procure.

title: Proverbs 21:26
text: V. 26. Coveteth-Spends his whole time in vain and lazy desires. Giveth-By God's blessing upon his industry he procures enough, not only for his own support, but for the relief of others.

title: Proverbs 21:27
text: V. 27. The sacrifice-All the most costly services which they offer to God.  Because-As all the ancient translators render it, the Hebrew particle, aph, being expletive: or, even because; so the following clause gives the reason.  A wicked mind-Not in obedience to God's command, but either to cover, or countenance, or promote some wicked design.

title: Proverbs 21:28
text: V. 28. Heareth-He witnesses nothing but what he has heard or seen. Constantly-Always affirms the same thing.

title: Proverbs 21:29
text: V. 29. Hardeneth-Continues in evil with obstinacy and impudence. Directs-He orders his steps aright.

title: Proverbs 21:31
text: V. 31. The horse-Under which all war-like provisions are comprehended.

title: Proverbs 22:1
text:
CHAP. XXII. 
 
  V. 1. Favour-A good report among men, especially good men, and that hearty kindness which attends it.

title: Proverbs 22:2
text: V. 2. Meet-They live together, and need one another.  The maker-Not only as they are men, but as they are poor or rich, which difference comes from God's providence.  They have one common creator, and Lord, and judge, and the one cannot despise nor grudge at the other without reflecting upon God.

title: Proverbs 22:3
text: V. 3. The evil-The judgment of God threatened, and approaching. Hideth-Retires to his strong tower, by prayer and repentance, puts himself under the protection of the almighty.  Pass on-Carefully and securely.

title: Proverbs 22:6
text: V. 6. Depart-Not easily and ordinarily.

title: Proverbs 22:7
text: V. 7. Is servant-Is at his mercy, and forced to comply with his pleasure.

title: Proverbs 22:8
text: V. 8. The rod-That power which he used with fury shall be taken from him.

title: Proverbs 22:9
text: V. 9. He-Who looks upon the wants and miseries of others with compassion.

title: Proverbs 22:12
text: V. 12. Preserve-God by the watchful eye of his providence maintains and defends.  Knowledge-Men of knowledge, knowing and good men. The matters-All his hopes, enterprizes, and concerns.

title: Proverbs 22:14
text: V. 14. The mouth-Her fair and flattering speeches.

title: Proverbs 22:15
text: V. 15. Bound-Is fixed and settled there, as being born with him, and rooted in his very nature.

title: Proverbs 22:16
text: V. 16. That giveth-That prodigally casts away his estate upon those who do not need it.

title: Proverbs 22:17
text: V. 17. My knowledge-The knowledge of God, which I am here delivering.

title: Proverbs 22:18
text: V. 18. Fitted-Fitly expressed: thou wilt be able to discourse profitably of them.

title: Proverbs 22:20
text: V. 20. In counsels and knowledge-In counsels which proceed from found knowledge.

title: Proverbs 22:21
text: V. 21. Answer-That thou mayst be able to give solid, and satisfactory answers.

title: Proverbs 22:22
text: V. 22. In the gate-Under pretence of justice.

title: Proverbs 22:23
text: V. 23. Spoil the soul-Take away not only their goods but their lives too.

title: Proverbs 22:29
text: V. 29. Before kings-He is fit to be employed in the affairs of princes.

title: Proverbs 23:1
text:
CHAP. XXIII. 
 
  V. 1. Ruler-With a great man.

title: Proverbs 23:2
text: V. 2. Put a knife-Restrain thine appetite, as if a man stood with a knife at thy throat.

title: Proverbs 23:3
text: V. 3. Deceitful-They do not yield thee that satisfaction which thou didst expect from them.

title: Proverbs 23:4
text: V. 4. Thine own wisdom-From worldly wisdom, which persuades men to use all possible means to get riches.

title: Proverbs 23:5
text: V. 5. Set thine eyes-Look upon it with earnestness and desire. Is not-Which has no solid and settled being.  Eagle-Swiftly, strongly, and irrecoverably.

title: Proverbs 23:6
text: V. 6. Evil eye-Of the envious or covetous man.

title: Proverbs 23:7
text: V. 7. So is he-You are not to judge of him by his words, but by the constant temper of his mind.

title: Proverbs 23:8
text: V. 8. Vomit up-When thou perceivest his churlish disposition, his meat will be loathsome to thee.  Sweet words-Thy pleasant discourse wherewith thou didst design to delight and profit him.

title: Proverbs 23:9
text: V. 9. Of a fool-Cast not away good counsels upon incorrigible sinners.

title: Proverbs 23:10
text: V. 10. Enter not-To possess their lands.

title: Proverbs 23:11
text: V. 11. Redeemer-Heb. their near kinsman, to whom it belongs to avenge their wrongs, and to recover and maintain their rights.

title: Proverbs 23:13
text: V. 13. Shall not die-It is a likely way to prevent his destruction.

title: Proverbs 23:16
text: V. 16. My reins-I shall rejoice with all my soul.

title: Proverbs 23:18
text: V. 18. An end-An expected and happy end for such as fear God.

title: Proverbs 23:19
text: V. 19. Guide-Order the whole course of thine affections and actions. In the way-In God's way.

title: Proverbs 23:23
text: V. 23. Buy-Purchase it upon any terms, spare no pains or cost. Truth-The true and saving knowledge of God's will.  Sell it not-Do not forsake it for any worldly advantage.

title: Proverbs 23:26
text: V. 26. Give me-Solomon here speaks in God's name.

title: Proverbs 23:30
text: V. 30. Mixt wine-Either mixed with water, or with other ingredients to make it strong and delicious.

title: Proverbs 23:31
text: V. 31. Red-Which was the colour of the best wines in that country. Aright-When it sparkles, and seems to smile upon a man.

title: Proverbs 23:34
text: V. 34. Lieth down-To sleep.  Sea-In a ship in the midst of the sea.

title: Proverbs 23:35
text: V. 35. Sick-I was not sensible of it.  Again-At present my condition requires sleep to settle myself, and when I am composed, I purpose to return to my former course.

title: Proverbs 24:2
text:
CHAP. XXIV. 
 
  V. 2. Destruction-How they may oppress and destroy others.

title: Proverbs 24:3
text: V. 3. Through wisdom-There is no need that thou shouldest raise thy family by ruining others, which thou mayest more effectually do by wisdom.

title: Proverbs 24:4
text: V. 4. By knowledge-Which in scripture phrase includes the love and practice of what we know.

title: Proverbs 24:5
text: V. 5. Is strong-Is courageous and resolute, and able by wisdom to do greater things than others can accomplish by strength.

title: Proverbs 24:6
text: V. 6. Thy war-War is better managed by wisdom than by strength.

title: Proverbs 24:7
text: V. 7. A fool-For a wicked man, whose sins enfeeble his mind, and make it incapable of wisdom.  Openeth not-He knows not how to speak acceptably, and profitably in the publick assembly.

title: Proverbs 24:8
text: V. 8. Shall be called-Though he cover his wicked devices with fair pretences, he shall be branded with that infamy which is due to him.

title: Proverbs 24:9
text: V. 9. The thought-The very inward thought or contrivance of evil, is a sin in God's sight.

title: Proverbs 24:11
text: V. 11. Deliver-When it is in thy power.  Drawn-By the violence of lawless men.

title: Proverbs 24:12
text: V. 12. Consider-That this is only a frivolous excuse.

title: Proverbs 24:13
text: V. 13. Eat-This is not a command, but a concession, and is only here expressed to illustrate the following verse.  Honey in those parts was an usual food.

title: Proverbs 24:14
text: V. 14. A reward-It is not only sweet for the present, but brings a sure and everlasting reward.

title: Proverbs 24:16
text: V. 16. Falleth-Into calamities, of which he evidently speaks both in the foregoing verse, and in the following branch of this verse. Fall-Frequently into irrecoverable destruction.

title: Proverbs 24:17
text: V. 17. Falleth-Into mischief.

title: Proverbs 24:18
text: V. 18. From him-Understand, upon thee, which is implied in the Hebrew phrase.

title: Proverbs 24:20
text: V. 20. No reward-All his happiness shall quickly and eternally perish. The candle-All their comfort and glory shall cease.

title: Proverbs 24:21
text: V. 21. To change-That are unstable in their obedience to God or to the king.

title: Proverbs 24:22
text: V. 22. Who knoweth-Who can conceive how sore and sudden will be the ruin of them that fear not God, and the king.

title: Proverbs 24:23
text: V. 23. These-The counsels following, to the end of the chapter, no less than those hitherto mentioned, are worthy of their consideration.

title: Proverbs 24:25
text: V. 25. Rebuke-That publickly and judicially rebuke and condemn the wicked.  Delight-The peace of a good conscience.

title: Proverbs 24:26
text: V. 26. Shall kiss-Shall respect him.  A right answer-That speaks pertinently and plainly, and truly.

title: Proverbs 24:32
text: V. 32. Received-I learned wisdom by his folly.

title: Proverbs 25:1
text:
CHAP. XXV. 
 
  V. 1. These-Which are contained in this and the following chapters. The men-Certain persons appointed by Hezekiah for that work.  Many of them are political precepts, and such as in a special manner concerned Hezekiah, and other princes, for the conduct of their house and kingdom. Copied-Out of the historical records which were then extant.

title: Proverbs 25:2
text: V. 2. The glory-It is agreeable to the nature of God; it is a testimony of his infinite wisdom, and of his absolute power and sovereignty. To conceal-To keep his counsels, and the reasons of his actions in his own breast.  Search out-To communicate their counsels to others, that so they may search and find out the right way.

title: Proverbs 25:3
text: V. 3. The heart-Though wise kings will search out other men, yet their inward thoughts and purposes are hardly discoverable.

title: Proverbs 25:4
text: V. 4. Take away-Then, and not 'till then it is fit for that use.

title: Proverbs 25:6
text: V. 6. Stand not-Do not affect frequent and familiar society with greater persons than thyself.

title: Proverbs 25:9
text: V. 9. Debate-If thou hast any quarrel with him, first try to compose it by private discourse with him.  Discover not-Let not heat of contention provoke thee to divulge any of his secrets committed to thy trust.

title: Proverbs 25:10
text: V. 10. Lest he-Reproach thee for thy gross violation of the laws of prudence, justice and friendship.

title: Proverbs 25:11
text: V. 11. Of silver-Which it seems was usual in those times, and was grateful to the eye for the beauty and variety both of the colours and figures, the golden apples appearing through net-work of silver.

title: Proverbs 25:13
text: V. 13. Cold of snow-As drink cooled with ice or snow, as is usual in hot countries.

title: Proverbs 25:14
text: V. 14. Boasteth-Promising what he never intends to  give. Is like-Like empty clouds carried about with wind, and not affording that rain which they promise.

title: Proverbs 25:15
text: V. 15. Forbearing-By patient submission and expectation. Breaketh-Softens the hardest heart.

title: Proverbs 25:16
text: V. 16. Honey-By honey he understands, not only all delicious meats, but all worldly delights, which we are here taught to use with moderation.

title: Proverbs 25:17
text: V. 17. Withdraw-Visit him not too frequently.

title: Proverbs 25:18
text: V. 18. A sword-Is as cruel and pernicious as any instrument of death.

title: Proverbs 25:20
text: V. 20. As vinegar-Which dissolves the nitre, and makes it useless and ineffectual.

title: Proverbs 25:21
text: V. 21. Bread-By bread and water he understands all things necessary for his subsistence.

title: Proverbs 25:22
text: V. 22. For-In so doing, which words are expressed  Romans 12:20 , where this text is quoted.  Thou shalt melt him into repentance, and love.

title: Proverbs 25:25
text: V. 25. So-Because it comes more rarely and difficultly, after it hath been long expected.

title: Proverbs 25:26
text: V. 26. Falling-When righteous men are oppressed by the wicked, the state of that common-wealth is as deplorable, as if the publick fountains were corrupted.

title: Proverbs 25:27
text: V. 27. Not good-For health.  To search-Industriously to seek for applause.  Is not-Is not only sinful, but shameful also.

title: Proverbs 26:2
text:
CHAP. XXVI. 
 
  V. 2. By flying-Secures itself from the fowler.  Not come-Upon the innocent person, but he shall escape from it like a bird.

title: Proverbs 26:4
text: V. 4. According-So as to imitate his folly, by passionate or reproachful speeches.

title: Proverbs 26:5
text: V. 5. According-So as his folly needs and requires, convincing him strongly, reproving him sharply, and exposing him to just shame.

title: Proverbs 26:6
text: V. 6. Cutteth off the feet-Of his messenger; bids one go that wants legs.  Drinketh-Drinking, in scripture, frequently denotes the plentiful doing or receiving of any thing.

title: Proverbs 26:7
text: V. 7. The legs-Heb. the legs of the lame are lifted up, in going, or in dancing, which is done with great inequality and uncomeliness. So-No less incident are wise and pious speeches from a foolish and ungodly man.

title: Proverbs 26:8
text: V. 8. Bindeth-Whereby he hinders his own design of throwing the stone out of it.  So-No less absurd is he that giveth to a fool that honour which he is not capable of using aright.

title: Proverbs 26:9
text: V. 9. A thorn-As a thorn is in a drunkard's hand, which he cannot manage cautiously, but employs to his own and others hurt. So-As unprofitable, and, by accident, hurtful to himself and others.

title: Proverbs 26:10
text: V. 10. Rewardeth-Will certainly give that recompence which is deserved by fools and transgressors, by such as sin either thro' ignorance, or wilfully.

title: Proverbs 26:14
text: V. 14. Turneth-Moving hither and thither upon it, but not removing from its place.

title: Proverbs 26:16
text: V. 16. A reason-A satisfactory reason of ail their actions.

title: Proverbs 26:17
text: V. 17. He-Who is going upon the way.  With strife-In which he is not concerned, nor any way obliged to meddle.  That taketh-Exposes himself to needless hazard.

title: Proverbs 26:18
text: V. 18. And death-Any instruments of death.

title: Proverbs 26:23
text: V. 23. Burning-With malice or hatred: A slanderous or evil tongue. Dross-Such a tongue and heart are of no real worth, although sometimes they make a shew of it, as dross does of silver.

title: Proverbs 26:26
text: V. 26. Deceit-With false professions of love.

title: Proverbs 26:27
text: V. 27. Rolleth-Up the hill with design to do mischief to some person.

title: Proverbs 27:1
text:
CHAP. XXVII. 
 
  V. 1. Boast not-Of any good thing which thou purposeth to do, or hopest to receive tomorrow, or hereafter.  Knowest not-What may happen in the space of one day.  The day is said to bring forth, what God by his almighty power either causes or suffers to be brought forth or done in it.

title: Proverbs 27:3
text: V. 3. Heavier-More grievous, being without cause, without measure, and without end.

title: Proverbs 27:5
text: V. 5. Open-When it is needful, in which case, though it put a man to some shame yet it doth him good.  Better-More desirable and beneficial. Secret love-Which does not shew itself by friendly actions, and particularly by free and faithful reproof.

title: Proverbs 27:6
text: V. 6. Wounds-The sharpest reproofs.  Kisses-All the outward profession of friendship.

title: Proverbs 27:8
text: V. 8. Wandereth-That flies from place to place, whereby she is exposed to all the arts of fowlers, and to birds of prey.  So-So is he who through vanity or lightness changes his abode, or his calling.

title: Proverbs 27:10
text: V. 10. Neither go-For comfort and relief, so as to forsake thy friend for him.  A neighbour-The friend, who hath shewed himself to be a good neighbour.  Near-In affection.

title: Proverbs 27:11
text: V. 11. Reproacheth-For being the father of a wicked son.

title: Proverbs 27:14
text: V. 14. Blesseth-That praises him to his face.  A loud voice-That both he, and others, may be sure to take notice of it.  Rising early-To shew his great forwardness.  A curse-His friend will value this kind of blessing no more than a curse.

title: Proverbs 27:16
text: V. 16. Hideth-Attempts to smother her passion.  Right-hand-Which being the great instrument of action, by its much stirring, diffuses the savour of it.

title: Proverbs 27:17
text: V. 17. Iron-Iron tools are made sharp and fit for use, by rubbing them against the file, or some other iron.  The countenance-The company or conversation of his friend.

title: Proverbs 27:18
text: V. 18. So he-That serves him faithfully, prudently, and diligently.

title: Proverbs 27:19
text: V. 19. So-So one man resembles another in the corruption of his nature.

title: Proverbs 27:20
text: V. 20. Hell-The grave devours all the bodies which are put into it, and is always ready to receive and devour more.  The eyes-The desires, which discover themselves by the eyes.

title: Proverbs 27:21
text: V. 21. To his praise-Or, according to his praise. So a man is tried by praise.

title: Proverbs 27:23
text: V. 23. Flock-Flocks and herds are here put for all possessions, because anciently they were the chief part of a man's riches.

title: Proverbs 27:24
text: V. 24. For-What thou dost now possess, will not last always.  If a man had the wealth of a kingdom, without care and diligence it would be brought to nothing.

title: Proverbs 27:25
text: V. 25. The hay-Another encouragement to diligence; God invites thee to it by the plentiful provisions wherewith he has enriched the earth for thy sake.  The mountains-Even the most barren parts afford thee their help.

title: Proverbs 27:26
text: V. 26. The price-By the sale whereof thou mayest either pay the rent of the field which thou hirest, or purchase fields or lands.  Goats might better be spared and sold than sheep, which brought a more constant profit to the owner.

title: Proverbs 27:27
text: V. 27. Goat's milk-Or, if thou chusest rather to keep thy goats, the milk will serve thee for food to thyself and family.  In ancient times men used a plain and simple diet.

title: Proverbs 28:2
text:
CHAP. XXVIII. 
 
  V. 2. But-By a wise and good prince.

title: Proverbs 28:3
text: V. 3. It like-Is like a violent rain or flood, which washes away the very seeds in the earth.  He is the worst of all oppressors.

title: Proverbs 28:4
text: V. 4. Contend-Are so far from praising them, that they severely reprove them.

title: Proverbs 28:5
text: V. 5. Judgment-What is just and right.  All things-Which are necessary to be known by them.

title: Proverbs 28:6
text: V. 6. Better-In a much happier condition.

title: Proverbs 28:10
text: V. 10. Causeth-That by evil counsel, or example, or artifice, draws them into evil.

title: Proverbs 28:12
text: V. 12. Rejoice-Are promoted.  Glory-In that common-wealth. Rise-Are advanced to authority.  Hidden-Wise and good men, who only are worthy of the name of men, withdraw themselves into obscure places.

title: Proverbs 28:14
text: V. 14. Alway-In all times, companies, and conditions.

title: Proverbs 28:16
text: V. 16. Oppressor-The tyranny of a prince, is a manifest sign of folly. Prolong-By God's favour, the peace and satisfaction of his own mind, and the hearty love of his people.

title: Proverbs 28:17
text: V. 17. Violence-That sheddeth any man's blood.  Shall flee-Shall speedily be destroyed.  Shall slay-None should desire or endeavour to save him from his deserved punishment.

title: Proverbs 28:18
text: V. 18. At once-Once for all; so he shall never rise more.

title: Proverbs 28:20
text: V. 20. Faithful-Who deals truly and justly in all his transactions.

title: Proverbs 28:21
text: V. 21. For-When a man hath once accustomed himself to take bribes, a very small advantage will make him sell justice.

title: Proverbs 28:22
text: V. 22. Evil eye-Is uncharitable to persons in want, and envious to those who get any thing besides him.  Poverty-And consequently that he shall need the pity and help of others.

title: Proverbs 28:24
text: V. 24. The same-Is a thief and robber.

title: Proverbs 28:25
text: V. 25. Fat-Shall live happily and comfortably.

title: Proverbs 28:26
text: V. 26. Wisely-Distrusting his own judgment, and seeking the advice of others, and especially of God.

title: Proverbs 28:28
text: V. 28. Men-Righteous men are afraid to appear publickly.

title: Proverbs 29:4
text:
CHAP. XXIX. 
 
  V. 4. Judgment-By the free and impartial exercise of justice. Gifts-Bribes.

title: Proverbs 29:8
text: V. 8. Wrath-The wrath of God or of men, who were enraged against it.

title: Proverbs 29:9
text: V. 9. Whether-Whether he, the wise man, deal sharply with him, or mildly, there is no rest, no end or fruit of the debate.

title: Proverbs 29:10
text: V. 10. Seek-To preserve it.

title: Proverbs 29:15
text: V. 15. Left-Suffered to follow his own will without restraint and chastening.

title: Proverbs 29:18
text: V. 18. No vision-No prophecy; no publick preaching of God's word.

title: Proverbs 29:19
text: V. 19. A servant-Who is so not only in condition, but also in the temper of his mind, disingenuous, and stubborn.  Words-By mere words. Tho'-Though he know thy mind, and his own duty.

title: Proverbs 29:20
text: V. 20. Hasty-Who is rash and heady in the management of his affairs.

title: Proverbs 29:21
text: V. 21. Delicately-Allowing him too much freedom, and familiarity. A son-Will find him at last grow insolent, and forgetful of his servile condition.

title: Proverbs 29:24
text: V. 24. Bewrayeth it not-Which he is bound to do for the publick good.

title: Proverbs 29:25
text: V. 25. A snare-Is an occasion of many sins.

title: Proverbs 29:26
text: V. 26. Judgment-The decision of his cause, and the success of all his endeavours.

title: Proverbs 30:1
text:
CHAP. XXX. 
 
  V. 1. Jakeh-Who lived either in Solomon's time, or rather afterwards, and was famous in his generation for wisdom and piety. The prophecy-The prophetical instruction; for as the prophets were public preachers as well as foretellers of things to come, so their sermons, no less than their predictions, are commonly called their prophecies.  And Ucal-Two friends and co-temporaries of Agur, who desired his instructions.

title: Proverbs 30:2
text: V. 2. Surely-This he utters from a modest and humble apprehension of his own ignorance.

title: Proverbs 30:3
text: V. 3. I neither learned-I have not been taught in the schools of wisdom.  Of the holy-Of the holy prophets.  I have not such Divine inspirations as prophets strictly so called have received.

title: Proverbs 30:4
text: V. 4. Who-What mere man?  None at all.  Ascended-To learn the mind of God who dwells there.  Descended-To teach men below what he had learned above.  No man can fully know and teach us these things unless he hath been in heaven, and sent down from thence to the earth for that end.  In his fists-To hold them in, or let them out at his pleasure? And none but he who made and governs all creatures, can know and teach these things.  The waters-Those above the clouds, and those below, the sea which God keeps as it were within doors, and the water which he shuts up in the bowels of the earth.  The earth-The whole earth from one end to another, which God upholdeth in the air, by the word of his power. If-If thou thinkest there be any man who can do these things, produce his name; or if he be dead, the name of any of his posterity.

title: Proverbs 30:5
text: V. 5. Pure-You must not expect the full knowledge of Divine mysteries from me, nor from any man, but from the word of God.

title: Proverbs 30:8
text: V. 8. Vanity-All vanity of heart and life; a vain conversation, or a love of the vain things of this world.  Lies-All falsehood and deceit in my words and carriage.  Convenient-Moderate and suitable both to my natural necessities, and to that condition of life in which thou hast put me.

title: Proverbs 30:9
text: V. 9. Deny thee-By trusting to riches, which is a denial of God, and by unthankfulness for, and abuse of his mercies.  Who is the Lord-That I should serve him.  Lest I take-Use false oaths either to vindicate myself when I am suspected, or to gratify others, as poor men frequently do.

title: Proverbs 30:10
text: V. 10. Accuse not-Without sufficient cause: for otherwise, in some cases this may be a duty.  Curse thee-Desire God to punish thee. Guilty-By God, who is ready to plead the cause of the afflicted.

title: Proverbs 30:11
text: V. 11. A generation-A sort of men.

title: Proverbs 30:12
text: V. 12. Not washed-Who imagine they are truly religious, when they live in a course of wickedness.

title: Proverbs 30:14
text: V. 14. Devour-Extortioners, and cruel oppressors.

title: Proverbs 30:15
text: V. 15. The horse-leach-An insatiable creature, sucking blood 'till it is ready to burst.  Two daughters-The following things resemble the horse-leach in its insatiableness; nothing being more ordinary than to call those persons or things the sons or daughters of those whose examples they imitate.  Three-Though he begins with two, yet he proceeds from thence to three, and four, all which are said to be the daughters of the horse-leach.

title: Proverbs 30:17
text: V. 17. The eye-He that scorneth or derideth his parents, tho' it be but with a look or gesture, and much more when he breaks out into opprobrious words and actions.

title: Proverbs 30:18
text: V. 18. Wonderful-The way whereof I cannot trace.

title: Proverbs 30:20
text: V. 20. Such is-So secret and undiscernible.  Eateth-The bread of deceit in secret.

title: Proverbs 30:21
text: V. 21. Four-Which are intolerable in human societies.

title: Proverbs 30:22
text: V. 22. A servant-For such an one is commonly ignorant, and therefore commits many errors; he is poor, and therefore insatiable, he is proud and imperious, and usually injurious and cruel.  A fool-A conceited fool. When-When he abounds in wealth.

title: Proverbs 30:23
text: V. 23. An odious-Proud, and perverse.  Married-For then she displays all those ill humours, which before, she concealed. Is heir-Which great and sudden change transports her beside herself, and makes her insufferably proud and scornful.

title: Proverbs 30:27
text: V. 27. Bands-Several companies, in exact order.

title: Proverbs 30:28
text: V. 28. Hands-With her legs, which he calls hands, because they serve her for the same use, to do her work, to weave her web, and to catch gnats or flies.  Palaces-Is not only in poor cottages, but many times in palaces also.

title: Proverbs 30:31
text: V. 31. An he-goat-Which marches in the head of the flock in a grave and stately manner, conducting them with great courage and resolution, and being ready to fight for them, either with beasts or men that oppose him.  A king-Heb. a king and his people with him, a king when he hath the hearts and hands of his people going along with him in his undertakings.

title: Proverbs 30:32
text: V. 32. Thought-Designed any injury against thy neighbour. Lay thine hand-Do not open thy mouth to excuse it, but repent of it, and do so no more.

title: Proverbs 30:33
text: V. 33. The forcing-The stirring up of wrath, either in a man's self towards others, by giving way to passion; or in others by reproaches, or any other provocations.  Bringeth forth-Is the cause of many quarrels.

title: Proverbs 31:1
text:
CHAP. XXXI. 
 
  An exhortation to Lemuel, ver. 1-9.   A description of good wife, ver. 10-31. 
 
  V. 1. Lemuel-Of Solomon, by the general consent both of Jewish and Christian writers; this name signifies one from God, or belonging to God, and such an one was Solomon eminently, being given by God to David and Bathsheba, as a pledge of his reconciliation to them after their repentance.  Possibly his mother gave him this name to mind him of his great obligations to God, and of the justice of his devoting himself to God's service.

title: Proverbs 31:2
text: V. 2. What-A short speech, arguing her great passion for him; what words shall I take?  What counsels shall I give thee?  My heart is full, but where shall I begin?  Of my womb-My son, not by adoption, but whom I bare in the womb, and therefore it is my duty to give thee admonitions, and thine to receive them.  My vows-On whose behalf I have made many prayers and sacrifices, and solemn vows to God; whom I have, as far as in me lay, devoted to the work, and service, and glory of God.

title: Proverbs 31:3
text: V. 3. Strength-The vigour of thy mind and body. Ways-Thy conversation, repeated in other words.

title: Proverbs 31:4
text: V. 4. To drink-To excess.

title: Proverbs 31:6
text: V. 6. To perish-To faint; for such need a cordial.

title: Proverbs 31:8
text: V. 8. The dumb-For such as cannot speak in their own cause, either through ignorance, or because of the dread of their more potent adversaries. Destruction-Who, without such succour from the judges, are like to be utterly ruined.

title: Proverbs 31:10
text: V. 10. A virtuous woman-Here he lays down several qualifications of an excellent wife, which are delivered in alphabetical order, each verse beginning with a several letter of the Hebrew alphabet.

title: Proverbs 31:11
text: V. 11. No need-He shall have no need to use indirect courses to get wealth.

title: Proverbs 31:13
text: V. 13. Flax-That she may find employment for her servants. Worketh-She encourages them to work by her example; which was a common practice among princesses in those first ages.  Not that it is the duty of kings and queens to use manual operations, but it is the duty of all persons, the greatest not excepted, to improve all their talents, and particularly their time, which is one of the noblest of them, to the service of that God to whom they must give an account, and to the good of that community to which they are related.

title: Proverbs 31:14
text: V. 14. From afar-By the sale of her home-spun commodities she purchases the choicest goods which come from far countries.

title: Proverbs 31:15
text: V. 15. Giveth-Distributes all necessary provisions.

title: Proverbs 31:16
text: V. 16. Considereth-Whether it be fit for her use.  The fruit-With the effects of her diligence.  Planteth-She improves the land to the best advantage.

title: Proverbs 31:17
text: V. 17. Girdeth-She uses great diligence and expedition in her employment; for which end, men in those times used to gird up their long and loose garments about their loins.  Strengtheneth-Puts forth her utmost strength in her business.

title: Proverbs 31:18
text: V. 18. Perceiveth-She finds great comfort in her labours. Her candle-Which is not to be taken strictly, but only signifies her unwearied care and industry.

title: Proverbs 31:19
text: V. 19. She layeth-By her own example she provokes her servants to labour.  And although in these latter and more delicate times, such mean employments are grown out of fashion among great persons, yet they were not so in former ages, neither in other countries, nor in this land; whence all women unmarried unto this day are called in the language of our law, Spinsters.

title: Proverbs 31:21
text: V. 21. Not afraid-Of any injuries of the weather.  Are clothed-She hath provided enough, not only for their necessity, but also for their delight and ornament.

title: Proverbs 31:22
text: V. 22. Tapestry-For the furniture of her house.  Silk-Which was agreeable to her high quality.

title: Proverbs 31:23
text: V. 23. It known-Observed and respected, not only for his own worth, but for his wife's sake.  Sitteth-In counsel or judgment.

title: Proverbs 31:24
text: V. 24. Girdles-Curiously wrought of linen, and gold, or other precious materials.

title: Proverbs 31:25
text: V. 25. Strength-Strength of mind, magnanimity, courage, activity. Her clothing-Her ornament and glory.  Rejoice-She lives in constant tranquillity of mind, from a just confidence in God's gracious providence.

title: Proverbs 31:26
text: V. 26. Openeth her mouth-She is neither sullenly silent, nor full of impertinent talk, but speaks discreetly and piously, as occasion offers. In her tongue-Her speeches are guided by wisdom and grace, and not by inordinate passions.  And this practice is called a law in her tongue, because it is constant and customary, and proceeds from an inward and powerful principle of true wisdom.

title: Proverbs 31:27
text: V. 27. Looketh well-She diligently observes the management of her domestick business, and the whole carriage of her children and servants.

title: Proverbs 31:30
text: V. 30. Favour-Comeliness, which commonly gives women favour with those who behold them.  Deceitful-It gives a false representation of the person, being often a cover to a deformed soul; it does not give a man that satisfaction, which at first he promised to himself from it; and it is soon lost, not only by death, but by many diseases and contingencies.

title: Proverbs 31:31
text: V. 31. Give her-It is but just, that she should enjoy those praises which her labours deserve.  Let her works-If men be silent, the lasting effects of her prudence and diligence will trumpet forth her praises. In the gates-In the most publick and solemn assemblies.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:1
text:
NOTES                          ON              The Book of ECCLESIASTES. 
 
  Three things are to be observed concerning this book.    1. The author; who was Solomon, as is manifest both from the common   consent of Jewish and Christian writers, and from the express   words of the first verse.  That he wrote it in his old age, is more than   probable from divers passages in it, as, that he did it after his   buildings, chap. 2:4, which yet took up twenty years of his life,    I Kings 9:10 , and after some considerable enjoyment of them, and planting   of gardens, and orchards, and reaping the fruit of them, chap. 2:5,6,   and after long and much consideration and experience of all those methods   in which men expect to find happiness, chap. 7:27, &c.  So this book   was written by him, as a publick testimony of his repentance and   detestation of those wicked courses to which he had addicted himself:   wherein he followed the example of his father David, who, after his   sad fall, penned the fifty-first psalm.  And the truth of this opinion   may be confirmed by that expression,  II Chronicles 11:17 .  They walked in the   way of David and Solomon; that is, wherein they walked, both before   their falls, and after their repentance.    2. The method of it.  For whereas there are some passages in it which   seem impious; it must be considered, that it is in part dramatical; that   Solomon speaks most things in his own name, but some things in the names   of ungodly men, as is undeniably manifest both front the scope and   design of the book, as it is expressed both in the beginning and in the   conclusion of it, and from his serious and large disputation against   those wicked principles and courses.  And this way of writing is not   unusual among both sacred and profane writers.    3. The design of it; which is, to describe man's true happiness, and   the way leading to it.  This he does both negatively, proving, that it   is not to be found either in secular wisdom, or in sensual pleasures, or   in worldly greatness and glory, or in abundance of riches, or in a vain   profession of religion: and positively, shewing, that it is to be had   only in the fear of God and obedience to his laws, which alone can give   a man a chearful enjoyment of his present comforts, and an assurance of   his everlasting happiness. 
 
                        ECCLESIASTES.                           CHAP. I. 
 
  The title of the book, ver. 1.   The general doctrine, All is vanity, ver. 2, 3.   Proved from the shortness of life, and the perpetual changes of all   the creatures, ver. 4-7.   From the unsatisfying toil of men, and the return of the same things   over again, ver. 8-11.   The vanity of knowledge, ver. 12-18. 
 
  V. 1. The preacher-Who was not only a king, but also a teacher of God's people: who having sinned grievously in the eyes of all the world, thought himself obliged to publish his repentance, and to give publick warning to all, to avoid those rocks upon which he had split.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:2
text: V. 2. Vanity-Not only vain, but vanity in the abstract, which denotes extreme vanity.  Saith-Upon deep consideration and long experience, and by Divine inspiration.  This verse contains the general proposition, which he intends particularly to demonstrate in the following book.  All-All worldly things.  Is vanity-Not in themselves for they are God's creatures and therefore good in their kinds, but in reference to that happiness, which men seek and expect to find in them.  So they are unquestionably vain, because they are not what they seem to be, and perform not what they promise, but instead of that are the occasions of innumerable cares, and fears, and sorrows, and mischiefs.  Nay, they are not only vanity but vanity of vanities, the vainest vanity, vanity in the highest degree.  And this is redoubled, because the thing is certain, beyond all possibility of dispute.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:3
text: V. 3. What profit-What real and abiding benefit?  None at all.  All is unprofitable as to the attainment of that happiness which all men are enquiring after.  His labour-Heb. his toilsome labour, both of body and mind in the pursuit of riches, or pleasures, or other earthly things. Under the sun-In all worldly matters, which are usually transacted in the day time, or by the light of the sun.  By this restriction he implies that the happiness which in vain is sought for in this lower world, is really to be found in heavenly places and things.

title: Ecclesiastes 1:4
text: V. 4.
